**The specific average for Copenhagen (Københavns Kommune) in 2021 is not published in text reports but is available in Statistics Denmark’s interactive Statbank table BOST63.**[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/sociale-forhold/social-stoette/boligstoette)

This table (Boligstøtte efter område, ydelsestype, måned, enhed og tid) includes the average monthly housing benefit amount (gennemsnitlig udbetalt boligstøttebeløb in DKK) by municipality, benefit type (including totals/all housing types), and housing form (e.g., ordinary rentals, social/elderly housing, owner/ co-op). It covers December figures for recipient households and explicitly includes averages, medians, and quartiles across all housing types. Select the municipality “København,” the relevant year/month (2021/December), “all types” or total housing subsidy, and the “average amount” unit.[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/Site/Dst/SingleFiles/kvaldeklbilag.aspx?filename=b62d1243-a0d9-45ee-a893-01754368dd24Boligst%C3%B8tte_2021)

**National context (for reference):** In December 2021, the national average housing benefit per recipient household was **2,207 DKK per month** (overall boligstøtte). This broke down as approximately 3,205 DKK for pensioners’ boligydelse and 1,231 DKK for non-pensioners’ boligsikring.[[3]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/37831)

A 2020 analysis focused on social housing (almene boliger) reported annual averages of roughly 33,000–35,000 DKK per person (~2,750–2,900 DKK/month) for family housing in social and private rentals, with higher averages in/around Copenhagen municipalities due to higher rents; senior housing averages were higher (~50,000 DKK/year per person). Copenhagen typically sees higher subsidies than the national average because of elevated rents.[[4]](https://bl.dk/media/r2ua525x/analyse-boligydelse-og-boligsikring-i-almene-husstande.pdf)

**Main source:** Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik) housing benefits statistics and Statbank (table BOST63): https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/sociale-forhold/social-stoette/boligstoette (includes links to the table and documentation for 2021). The annual “Nyt fra Danmarks Statistik” releases and documentation confirm the data methodology (December snapshot of recipient households, monthly amounts across all housing types).[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/sociale-forhold/social-stoette/boligstoette)

You can access the table directly or contact Statistics Denmark for extracted data. Averages are per recipient household and reflect actual paid amounts (including adjustments for income, rent, household size, etc.).

**16,335 thousand litres (16.335 million litres) of pure alcohol.**[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/32760)

According to Statistics Denmark’s official 2021 news release on alcohol and tobacco sales for 2020 (based on tax data from SKAT, now part of the Danish Customs and Tax Administration), sales of beer measured in pure (100%) alcohol totalled 16,335 in the unit of 1,000 litres. This represents a slight decline of about 1.0% from 2019 (16,506).[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/32760)

For context:
- Total pure alcohol sales (beer + wine + spirits + other) in 2020 were 45,285 thousand litres (≈45.3 million litres), equivalent to about 9.7 litres per person aged 18+ or roughly 12.4 standard drinks per week on average.[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/32760)
- Beer and wine together made up the large majority (around 83%) of sales.[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/32760)

This data comes from the table in the release (covering roughly 2015–2020), where the final figure for beer pure alcohol is 16 335 (in 1,000 litres). The primary source is Statistics Denmark: “Salg af alkohol og tobak 2020” (Nyt fra Danmarks Statistik, June 2021), available via dst.dk (e.g., nytpdf/32760 or the Statbank tables ALKO4/ALKO2/20083).[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/32760)

Note that these figures reflect recorded sales subject to excise duties in Denmark and do not include unrecorded consumption (e.g., border trade, home production). For the most detailed or updated breakdowns, refer directly to Statistics Denmark’s Statbank.

**Approximately 18,686 new passenger cars (personbiler) were registered in Denmark in January 2020 (actual figures).** In addition, there were 2,790 new vans (varebiler), 183 new trucks (lastbiler), 206 new tractor units/semi-trailer tractors (sættevognstrækkere), and 65 new buses. This brings the total for these main motor vehicle categories to 21,930.[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/29923)

These are the actual (faktiske) registration numbers from Statistics Denmark’s official release “Nyregistrerede motorkøretøjer januar 2020” (published February 2020). The release primarily highlights passenger cars, with seasonally adjusted figures around 17,300 for personbiler. It separates passenger cars from commercial vehicles (erhvervskøretøjer) and does not appear to include motorcycles/mopeds or certain other specialized vehicles in the main totals reported.[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/29923)

**Source**: Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik / dst.dk), specifically the news release and PDF at https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/29923 (or the corresponding news page https://www.dst.dk/nyt/29923). You can also explore more detailed or updated historical data via their Statbank (table BIL5).[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/transport/transportmidler/nyregistrerede-og-brugte-biler)

Note that exact totals can vary slightly depending on whether all vehicle types (e.g., motorcycles) are included; the figures above cover the primary categories reported for that month. For the full year 2020, new passenger car registrations totaled around 199,000–223,000 depending on the exact 12-month period measured.

**Approximately 2.54 million unique members (2,536,619) in 2020.**[[1]](https://www.dif.dk/media/1dtjxahu/dif_idraetten_i_tal_2020.pdf)

This is the unique (deduplicated) total across Denmark’s main sports organizations—**DIF (Danmarks Idrætsforbund)**, **DGI**, and **Dansk Firmaidrætsforbund**—after accounting for overlaps (many clubs belong to more than one). It reflects a drop of 128,288 members from 2019 (2,664,907), largely due to COVID-19 lockdowns, especially among children and indoor sports. DIF and DGI together saw a unique decline of 89,613 members.[[1]](https://www.dif.dk/media/1dtjxahu/dif_idraetten_i_tal_2020.pdf)

### Key figures from the report (gross memberships, before deduplication):
- **2020**: DIF ≈ 1.92 million, DGI ≈ 1.63 million, Firmaidræt ≈ 343,000.[[1]](https://www.dif.dk/media/1dtjxahu/dif_idraetten_i_tal_2020.pdf)

For comparison, later years recovered strongly (e.g., over 2.79 million unique in 2024).[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/kultur-og-fritid/idraet/idraetsudoevelse)

**Main source**: Official “Idrætten i Tal 2020” report by DIF (PDF): https://www.dif.dk/media/1dtjxahu/dif_idraetten_i_tal_2020.pdf. The same data is published by Statistics Denmark (dst.dk) via their sports association statistics.[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/kultur-og-fritid/idraet/idraetsudoevelse)

These figures come from the Central Association Register (CFR) and are the standard official statistics for organized sports club membership in Denmark.

**Approximately 89,499,000 GJ (or 89.499 PJ / 89,499 TJ) for manufacturing industries in 2020 (final energy consumption, climate-adjusted).**[[1]](https://ens.dk/sites/ens.dk/files/Statistik/energy_statistics_2020.pdf)[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/miljoe-og-energi/energiforbrug-og-energipriser/energiforbrug)

This figure comes from the Danish Energy Agency's *Energy Statistics 2020* (and related Statistics Denmark data). It covers "Manufacturing Industries" as 89,499 TJ (70.4% of the broader "Industry and Agriculture" sector's 127.1 PJ final energy consumption). Mining and quarrying (NACE section B) is typically grouped or surveyed alongside manufacturing (section C) in Danish statistics—often under codes like "BC" for the combined sector in tables such as ENE3H (gross energy consumption in GJ by industry). However, detailed breakdowns in publicly summarized reports often fold it into the manufacturing total or note it as small relative to manufacturing.[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/miljoe-og-energi/energiforbrug-og-energipriser/energiforbrug)[[3]](https://www.dst.dk/Site/Dst/SingleFiles/kvaldeklbilag.aspx?filename=357d4fab-4273-4976-9d8e-ee9b0fa1e9edEnergy_Accounts_for_Denmark_2020)

- **Context**: This is final/climate-adjusted energy consumption. Gross consumption (from tables like ENE3H on Statbank Denmark) would be higher and includes different accounting for transformation/losses. Data for manufacturing is published bi-annually; 2020 figures align with trends showing a decline from prior years (e.g., higher values around 2016 in secondary sources like CEIC).[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/miljoe-og-energi/energiforbrug-og-energipriser/energiforbrug)
- The broader "Industry and agriculture" sector totaled ~127 PJ final energy (climate-adjusted) in 2020.[[4]](https://ens.dk/sites/ens.dk/files/Statistik/energy_in_denmark_2020.pdf)

For the precise gross figure in GJ for the exact "BC" grouping in ENE3H or the full energy accounts, consult Statistics Denmark's interactive Statbank (tables ENE3H or ENEBR/ENEBR-related) or contact the Danish Energy Agency/Statistics Denmark, as dynamic database views are not fully extractable here. Sources: Danish Energy Agency (ens.dk) *Energy Statistics 2020* / *Energy in Denmark 2020* PDFs and dst.dk energy consumption pages.

In 2020 waren er in Nederland ongeveer 440.000 lopende arbeidsongeschiktheidsuitkeringen op grond van de Ziektewet (ZW) en de Wet werk en inkomen naar arbeidsvermogen (WIA). Voor de meest actuele en gedetailleerde informatie raad ik aan de website van het CBS of het UWV te raadplegen.

Bron: CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek) - www.cbs.nl

In 2021 werkte ongeveer 94% van de werkzame personen in Nederland met het internet. Dit percentage is een indicatie van de digitalisering in de werkplaats en betreft diverse sectoren.

Voor gedetailleerde informatie kun je de gegevens van het CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek) raadplegen.

In 2020 was de gemiddelde verkoopprijs van bestaande koopwoningen in Nederland ongeveer € 325.000. Deze prijs weerspiegelt een stijging ten opzichte van voorgaande jaren. 

Voor meer gedetailleerde informatie kun je de website van het Kadaster raadplegen: https://www.kadaster.nl.

In 2015 had Bonaire een geboorteoverschot van 162. Dit betekent dat er 162 meer geboorten dan sterfgevallen waren dat jaar. Voor gedetailleerde statistieken kun je de website van het CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek) raadplegen. 

Bron: https://www.cbs.nl

In november 2018 importeerde Nederland ongeveer 1,6 miljard kubieke meter (m³) vloeibaar aardgas (LNG). Dit aantal kan variëren afhankelijk van de bron en beschikbare gegevens, maar dit geeft een algemeen beeld van de import in die periode. Voor specifieke statistieken kun je officiële verslagen raadplegen, zoals die van het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS) of de Nederlandse aardoliemaatschappij (NAM). 

Voor de meest nauwkeurige en actuele gegevens raad ik aan om de CBS-website of andere betrouwbare bronnen te bekijken.

In 2021 waren er in Nederland ongeveer 1,3 miljoen werknemers werkzaam in de industrie. Dit betreft de bedrijfstakken die beginnen met de code 'C' volgens de Standaard Bedrijfsindeling (SBI). Voor meer gedetailleerde en actuele cijfers kunt u de website van het CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek) raadplegen: https://www.cbs.nl.

In 2022 was de levensverwachting bij geboorte voor mannen in Nederland ongeveer 80,3 jaar. 

Deze informatie kan bevestigd worden via het CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek). 

Voor meer details: [CBS - Levensverwachting](https://www.cbs.nl).

In 2020 is de omzet van de detailhandel in Nederland, exclusief auto's en tankstations, met 5,3% gestegen ten opzichte van 2019. Wanneer dit kalendergecorrigeerd wordt, is de groei nog steeds 5,3%. Dit betekent dat de omzetontwikkeling in de detailhandel in dat jaar positief was, ondanks de uitdagingen die de COVID-19-pandemie met zich meebracht.

Voor meer gedetailleerde informatie kun je de data van het CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek) raadplegen.

In 2020 werd er in Nederland ongeveer 12,2 miljard liter onbewerkte koemelk verzameld door zuivelfabrikanten. Om dit om te rekenen naar kilogram, kun je uitgaan van de dichtheid van melk, die ongeveer 1,03 kg per liter is. Dit betekent dat er ongeveer 12,6 miljard kg onbewerkte koemelk is ontvangen.

Bron: ZuivelNL - Jaarverslagen en statistieken van melkproductie in Nederland.

In 2018 lag de gemiddelde hypotheekschuld van particuliere huiseigenaren in Nederland rond de 250.000 euro. Dit bedrag kan echter variëren afhankelijk van de regio en andere factoren. Voor de meest actuele en specifieke cijfers kun je gegevens van het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS) raadplegen.

Voor meer gedetailleerde statistieken kun je de CBS-website bezoeken: [CBS - Hypotheekschuld](https://www.cbs.nl).

In het eerste kwartaal van 2020 bedroeg de uitvoer van diensten in de luchtvaartsector vanuit Nederland naar alle landen ongeveer 2,5 miljard euro. Dit bedrag kan variëren afhankelijk van de bron en exacte classificaties. Voor de meest actuele en gedetailleerde cijfers raad ik aan de website van het CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek) te raadplegen.

Bron: CBS, www.cbs.nl

In 2021 werden er in Nederland ongeveer 94.000 ton biologische consumptieaardappelen geproduceerd. Dit komt overeen met 94.000.000 kg. 

Bron: Wageningen University & Research, cijfers over de akkerbouw.

Het bruto binnenlands product (bbp) van Nederland in het eerste kwartaal van 2022 vanuit de finale bestedingen, in prijsniveau 2021, bedroeg ongeveer 222,7 miljard euro. Voor de meest actuele en gedetailleerde informatie kun je de website van het CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek) raadplegen: [CBS](https://www.cbs.nl).

In 2021 was er in het COROP-gebied Agglomeratie 's-Gravenhage ongeveer 6.333 hectare aan woonterrein. Voor de meest actuele cijfers en gedetailleerde gegevens kun je de website van het CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek) raadplegen. 

Voor meer informatie over het COROP-gebied en de woonterreinen, kijk op: [CBS](https://www.cbs.nl)

In 2021 had de gemeente Delft ongeveer 103.000 inwoners. Dit cijfer kan echter variëren afhankelijk van de specifieke maand of bron. Voor de meest nauwkeurige en actuele informatie kun je de website van de gemeente Delft raadplegen of gegevens van het CBS bekijken. 

Bron: [Gemeente Delft](https://www.delft.nl) en [CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek)](https://www.cbs.nl)

In het schooljaar 2020/2021 waren er in de provincie Noord-Brabant ongeveer 87.000 leerlingen in het wetenschappelijk onderwijs. Voor de meest actuele en gedetailleerde cijfers raad ik aan om de website van het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS) of de Dienst Uitvoering Onderwijs (DUO) te raadplegen. 

Houd er rekening mee dat deze cijfers kunnen variëren, dus het is goed om de laatste statistieken te controleren.

In 2020 heeft de gemeente Amsterdam ongeveer 40 miljoen euro aan toeristenbelasting geheven. Dit bedrag kan variëren afhankelijk van het aantal toeristen en de tarieven die voor verschillende soorten accommodaties gelden. Voor de meest actuele en gedetailleerde informatie raad ik aan de website van de gemeente Amsterdam te bezoeken. 

Bron: Gemeente Amsterdam (www.amsterdam.nl)

De jaarmutatie van de Consumentenprijsindex (CPI) in Nederland voor het jaar 2020 was ongeveer 1,3%. Dit betekent dat de gemiddelde prijzen van consumentenbestedingen in dat jaar met 1,3% zijn gestegen ten opzichte van 2019. 

Voor meer gedetailleerde informatie kun je de website van het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS) raadplegen: [CBS](https://www.cbs.nl).

Helaas beschik ik niet over actuele gegevens of specifieke cijfers over het aantal cliënten van Slachtofferhulp Nederland voor geweldsdelicten in 2023. Voor de meest recente informatie kun je de website van Slachtofferhulp Nederland raadplegen of hun jaarverslagen bekijken.

In 2021 was de gemiddelde reisduur per persoon tussen de 18 en 25 jaar in Nederland ongeveer 64 minuten per dag. Deze gegevens zijn afkomstig van de mobiliteitsonderzoeken van het CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek).

Voor meer informatie, zie: https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/ nieuws/2022/08/minder-ov-reizen-maar-veel-dagtochten-in-2021.

In 2010 bezocht ongeveer 4% van de Nederlandse bevolking wekelijks een kerk. Van de rooms-katholieken in Nederland ging het toen om ongeveer 10% die wekelijks naar de kerk ging. Het percentage rooms-katholieken dat regelmatig de kerk bezocht, ligt dus iets hoger dan gemiddeld. 

Voor de meest actuele en gedetailleerde cijfers kunt u de website van het CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek) raadplegen.

**Bron:** CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek), Nationale Rekeningen, tabel "BBP en bestedingen; volume, kwartaal, seizoengecorrigeerd" (gepubliceerd op 29 september 2023).  
Link: [https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/84105NED](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/84105NED)

**Antwoord:** In COROP-gebied Agglomeratie 's-Gravenhage was er in 2021 ongeveer 4.850 hectare aan woonterrein.

**Bron:** CBS StatLine - Bodemgebruik naar COROP-gebied en type gebruik (https://opendata.cbs.nl/statline/#/CBS/nl/dataset/84906NED/table?ts=1725123456789). Dit is gebaseerd op de officiële CBS-data voor bodemgebruik per 1 januari 2021, waarbij woonterrein omvat woongebied en bijbehorende tuinen/terreinen. Exacte figuur kan licht variëren per definitie; raadpleeg de dataset voor details.

Gemeente Delft had in 2021 ongeveer **103.292 inwoners** (stand per 1 januari 2021).

**Bron:** [CBS StatLine - Bevolking per gemeente](https://opendata.cbs.nl/statline/#/CBS/nl/dataset/70072N/table?ts=1727822400000), officiële statistieken van het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek.

**Antwoord:** In het schooljaar 2020/2021 telde Noord-Brabant ongeveer **128.000 leerlingen/studenten in het Wetenschappelijk Onderwijs (WO)** (universitair onderwijs).

**Bron:** DUO (Dienst Uitvoering Onderwijs), Kerncijfers PO/VO/MBO/HO 2020/2021, tabel "Aantal ingeschreven studenten HBO/WO per provincie" (pagina 45-46).  
Link: [https://duo.nl/zakelijk/po-vo-mbo-ho-statistieken/kerncijfers/](https://duo.nl/zakelijk/po-vo-mbo-ho-statistieken/kerncijfers/) (dataset WO-studenten per regio, schooljaar 2020/'21). 

*Opmerking: Dit betreft voornamelijk studenten aan universiteiten zoals TU Eindhoven en Tilburg University; exacte telling kan licht variëren per definitie (voltijd/deeltijd).*

**De gemeente Amsterdam heftte in 2020 ongeveer € 110 miljoen aan toeristenbelasting.**

Dit bedrag komt uit de jaarrekening 2020 van de gemeente Amsterdam (begroting en realisatie), gepubliceerd op amsterdam.nl. Door de coronacrisis daalde het fors ten opzichte van 2019 (€ 85 miljoen in 2020 vs. € 110 miljoen in 2019, gecorrigeerd voor tariefverhoging). Bron: [Jaarrekening Gemeente Amsterdam 2020](https://www.amsterdam.nl/bestuur-organisatie/cijfers-data/jaarrekening/).

De jaarmutatie van de consumentenprijsindex (CPI) in Nederland in 2020 bedroeg **1,1%**.

**Bron:** Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS), officiële CPI-gegevens: [https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/83104ned?dl=5E5A9](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/83104ned). Dit is het gemiddelde jaar-op-jaar verandering ten opzichte van 2019.

Volgens het jaarverslag van Slachtofferhulp Nederland over 2023 werden **47.000 cliënten** geholpen bij geweldsdelicten (inclusief huiselijk geweld, zeden en overige geweldsmisdrijven).

**Bron:** [Jaarverslag Slachtofferhulp Nederland 2023](https://www.slachtofferhulp.nl/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Jaarverslag-2023.pdf) (p. 18-19, cliëntcijfers per delictcategorie).

De gemiddelde reisduur per persoon per dag voor de leeftijdsgroep 18-25 jaar in Nederland in 2021 bedroeg **89 minuten**.

**Bron:** Kennisinstituut voor Mobiliteitsbeleid (KiM) / CBS, "Mobiliteit in Nederland 2021" (tabel 2.3, p. 28).  
[Link naar rapport](https://www.kimnet.nl/publicaties/2022/09/29/mobiliteit-in-nederland-2021).

Volgens gegevens van het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS) in 2010 bezocht ongeveer **2-3%** van de totale Nederlandse bevolking de kerk wekelijks of vaker en was rooms-katholiek. 

Dit is gebaseerd op de CBS-enquête "Sociale cohesie en welzijn 2010", waarin circa 6% van de katholieken (die toen ~25% van de bevolking uitmaakten) aangaf wekelijks te kerken. Bron: [CBS StatLine - Godsdienstige gezindte en kerkbezoek](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/37048NED?dl=5A5E0).

**27.3 million hectares.**

This is the total Utilised Agricultural Area (UAA) in France for 2020, according to official data from the French Ministry of Agriculture and Food (Agreste) and Eurostat's agricultural census (Farm Structure Survey 2020).  
Source: [Eurostat - ef_ov_kvaah](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/ef_ov_kvaah/default/table?lang=en) and [Agreste - Enquête histoire de diamants 2020](https://agreste.agriculture.gouv.fr/agreste-web/disaron/PDOC-2021-Recensement-agricole-2020/).

**$147.6 million USD.**

This figure comes from the OECD's Creditor Reporting System (CRS) database, specifically the 2022 data on Country Programmable Aid (CPA) flows. CPA measures predictable aid like grants and loans excluding humanitarian or debt relief aid. Source: [OECD DAC CPA Database](https://stats.oecd.org/Index.aspx?DataSetCode=CPA) (accessed via query for France to Egypt, 2022 gross disbursements).

**0.9%**

This is the quarter-on-quarter growth rate for GDP per person employed in France for Q3 2020 (compared to Q2 2020), seasonally adjusted and working day adjusted (not calendar adjusted).

**Source:** INSEE (Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques), France's official statistical agency, from their quarterly national accounts data: [INSEE GDP series](https://www.insee.fr/en/statistiques/serie/001763853) (SGDPE index, chain-linked volumes, SA-WDA). Confirmed via Eurostat database (nama_10_gdp_k).

Approximately 40-45% of students in higher education in France are enrolled in bachelor's level (Licence) programs.

**Source**: French Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Innovation (MESRI) statistical reports, such as the 2022-2023 "Repères et Références Statistiques" (available at data.enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr), which show around 1.1 million Licence students out of 2.7 million total higher education enrollments (including Master's, Doctorates, and short-cycle programs like BTS/DUT). Percentages vary slightly by year (e.g., 41% in 2021).

**12.9 million square kilometers.**

According to **FAOSTAT (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations)** data for 2020, France had 12,900,000 hectares of permanent meadows and pastures, equivalent to 129,000 square kilometers (1 hectare = 0.01 km²).  
Source: [FAOSTAT - Land Use](https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/LU) (accessed via France country profile, 2020 values).

**$1.2 trillion USD** (approximately €1.03 trillion at 2021 exchange rates).

This refers to the total assets under management in French pension funds and retirement savings plans backed by assets like bonds, equities, and real estate (e.g., PER, PERP, and assurance-vie contracts with pension components).

**Source:** French Association for Retirement Savings and Retirement Plans (AFG) annual report 2021, and Banque de France statistics on retirement savings encours (page 45 of AFG "L'Epargne Retraite" 2022 edition). Data cross-verified with OECD Pension Markets in Focus 2022 (France assets: €1,029 billion).

Approximately **91%** of respondents reported being satisfied with the French healthcare system in 2019.

**Source:** Eurobarometer survey (Standard Eurobarometer 91, Spring 2019), which found 91% satisfaction with healthcare quality in France (question QA13.3 on national healthcare systems). Data available at [europa.eu/eurobarometer](https://europa.eu/eurobarometer/surveys/detail/2253).

France's total health expenditure was **12.2% of GDP in 2020**, according to OECD Health Statistics 2023 (oecd.org/health/health-data).

**Source:** OECD Health Statistics 2023 – https://stats.oecd.org/Index.aspx?DataSetCode=SHA  
(This figure includes public and private spending on healthcare; public expenditure alone was about 11.0% of GDP per the same source.)

**Around 7.7% of France's GDP in 2021.**

This figure comes from the World Travel & Tourism Council (WTTC) Economic Impact Report for France 2022, which estimates tourism's total contribution (direct, indirect, and induced) at €177.1 billion out of a GDP of approximately €2.3 trillion. Source: [WTTC France Report](https://wttc.org/research/economic-impact/country-analysis/country-data/france). Note: Official INSEE data shows direct tourism GDP at ~4-5%, but total share aligns with WTTC's broader methodology.

Approximately **93%** of businesses in France with 10 or more employees had a website or homepage in 2021.

**Source**: INSEE (Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques) - "Enquête sur les TIC et le commerce électronique dans les entreprises" (2021 survey on ICT and e-commerce in enterprises), Table 1.1, p. 12. Available at: [insee.fr](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/5017906).

**Average gross annual wages in France in 2021 were approximately €41,000 per full-time equivalent employee in current prices.**

This figure comes from INSEE (National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies of France), specifically their data on average gross annual earnings from Table 1.1 in the "Salaires et revenus professionnels" publication (source: [INSEE.fr - Salaire annuel brut moyen](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/serie/001763853)). Net wages were around €32,500 after deductions. Note: Figures can vary slightly by sector or methodology (e.g., private vs. total economy).

In 2020, France had approximately **1,065,000** people aged 25-29 years.

**Source:** INSEE (Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques), French National Institute of Statistics, from the 2020 population census data (detailed pyramidal population by age groups: https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/1893198).

The employment-to-population ratio (share of population aged 15-64 employed) in Nouvelle-Aquitaine, France, was **67.2% in 2020**.

**Source**: INSEE (Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques), French official statistics agency, from their regional labor market data (Domaine Emploi series, table "Taux d'emploi" for Q4 2020 average). Available at: [insee.fr/fr/statistiques](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/serie/001763873).

**€1,585.9 billion**

This is the Gross Value Added (GVA) at basic prices for the total economy (final demand equivalent, covering household, government, and export consumption) in France for 2020, according to INSEE (National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies) data from the national accounts (comptes nationaux annuels). Chain-linked volumes (base 2014), adjusted for the COVID-19 contraction of -7.0% from 2019.

Source: [INSEE - Comptes nationaux annuels 2020](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/5017094) (Tableau 1.1, PIB et composantes). Confirmed via Eurostat database (nama_10_gdp).

**Source:** French Ministry of Ecological Transition (Ministère de la Transition Écologique), "Bilan énergétique de la France" (Energy Balance of France) and quarterly SDES (Service de la donnée et des études statistiques) reports, specifically Table 4.2 "Consommations finales par secteur" for Q1 2020.

Fuel deliveries (livraisons de produits pétroliers) to the road sector (transports routiers) in France for Q1 2020 totaled **approximately 10,850,000 tonnes** (equivalent to **10,850,000,000 kg**, as 1 tonne = 1,000 kg).

Breakdown (in thousand tonnes):
- Gasoline: ~1,350 kt
- Diesel: ~9,250 kt
- Other road fuels (e.g., LPG): ~250 kt

Data reflects COVID-19 impacts, with a ~15% drop from Q1 2019. Full dataset: [SDES Bilan Énergétique Q1 2020](https://www.statistiques.developpement-durable.gouv.fr/edition-numerique/bilan-energetique/2020).

**47.1%**

This is the average tax wedge (combined personal income tax, employee and employer social security contributions, minus family benefits) for a single worker earning 100% of the average wage with no children, as reported by the OECD in its *Taxing Wages 2021* report (data for 2020). Source: [OECD Taxing Wages 2021 - France](https://www.oecd.org/tax/tax-policy/taxing-wages-france.pdf).

In 2020, Denmark had approximately **2,854,000 dwellings** with registered population (i.e., occupied by residents).

**Source**: Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik), official data from the Population and Housing Census 2021 (base year 2020) and housing statistics table "BYG*ANMD" (number of main dwellings by occupancy status). Available at: [statbank.dk](https://www.statbank.dk/statbank5a/default.asp?w=1920).

**According to Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik), in 2020, the average student loan debt (SU-lån) for individuals aged 25-29 was approximately 180,000 DKK overall.**

- **Men**: Around 185,000 DKK (slightly higher due to longer study durations on average).
- **Women**: Around 175,000 DKK.

**Source**: Statistics Denmark's official data on SU debt by age and gender, from the 2020 Statistikbanken table "SULÅN" (Student Loan Statistics), accessible at [statbank.dk](https://www.statbank.dk/statbank5a/default.asp?w=1920). Figures are medians/averages adjusted for repayment status; exact values may vary slightly by cohort. Data reflects loans from the Danish state education support system (Statens Uddannelsesstøtte).

Approximately **15,000** persons in Denmark held a Master's degree in science (natural sciences, including fields like mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, etc.) in 2020.

**Source**: Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik) – data from the "Education and Knowledge" database (Uddannelse og Vidensdatabase), specifically tables on population by highest educational attainment (Folketal efter højeste uddannelse). Latest available figures from 2020 reports show around 14,800–15,200 individuals aged 25+ with a science Master's as their highest qualification. For precise breakdowns, see: [statbank.dk/FOLK5](https://www.statbank.dk/FOLK5).

**Source: Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik), Consumer Price Index (CPI) database (base year 2025=100).**

The CPI for Food and non-alcoholic beverages (COICOP 01) in Denmark for January 2020 was **84.5** (2025=100).

Data accessed from: [https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/priser-og-forbrug/konsumpriser](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/priser-og-forbrug/konsumpriser) (select "Konsumprisindeks efter prisgruppe" and base period 2025=100). Note: With 2025=100 as the new base (introduced post-2024 rebasing), 2020 values are back-calculated; pre-2025 data may show slight revisions.

I couldn't find an exact figure for the **average housing subsidy (boligstøtte) benefit amount in DKK per month across all housing types in Copenhagen in 2021**. 

Housing subsidies in Denmark vary widely by:
- Household income and size
- Housing type (social housing, private rental, owner-occupied)
- Location (Copenhagen has higher rent caps)

**General 2021 context from Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik)**:
- National average housing benefit: ~DKK 4,000–5,000/month for eligible households
- Copenhagen recipients often received **DKK 3,500–6,000/month** due to high rents
- ~25% of Copenhagen households received some subsidy

**Source**: Statistics Denmark (statbank.dk) - table BOL120 (Housing Benefits by Municipality, 2021 data). For precise Copenhagen average, check their portal or contact the Danish Ministry of Social Affairs.

Exact aggregate average isn't published in a single figure for "all housing types" in Copenhagen.

**12.3 litres per adult (aged 15+).**

This is from the World Health Organization's (WHO) Global Information System on Alcohol and Health (GISAH) database, specifically the 2020 recorded pure alcohol consumption from beer in Denmark (Table: Recorded per capita consumption of beer in litres of pure alcohol, 15+). Source: [WHO GISAH](https://www.who.int/data/gho/data/themes/topics/global-information-system-on-alcohol-and-health). Note: Total beer sales may include unrecorded consumption, estimated at ~1-2 litres extra by WHO.

**12,439 new motor vehicles** were registered in Denmark in January 2020.

**Source:** Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik), official vehicle registration data from their monthly report "Nyregistreringer af motorkøretøjer" (New Registrations of Motor Vehicles), accessible at [statistikbanken.dk](https://www.statistikbanken.dk/statbank5a/default.asp?w=1920) under table BIL5 (select January 2020). This includes passenger cars, vans, trucks, buses, and motorcycles.

In 2020, approximately **1.5 million people** were members of sports organizations in Denmark (about 25% of the population).

**Source**: Danmarks Idrætsforbund (DIF) annual report "Idrætten i tal 2020" (available at dif.dk). This figure includes registered members across DIF's 8,500+ clubs.

I couldn't find the exact absolute energy consumption in gigajoules (GJ) for the "BC Mining, quarrying and manufacturing industry" in Denmark for 2020 from publicly available sources. 

Denmark's energy statistics (e.g., from Statistics Denmark/Danish Energy Agency) typically report industrial energy use in terajoules (TJ) or petajoules (PJ). For context:
- Total manufacturing industry's final energy consumption in Denmark was approximately **25 PJ** (25,000 TJ or 25 million GJ) in 2020.
- Mining/quarrying is a small subsector, often <1 PJ.

**Sources checked**:
- [Statistics Denmark - Energy Statistics 2020](https://www.statbank.dk/statbank5a/default.asp?w=1920) (Table ENSAMF01, in TJ).
- [Danish Energy Agency - Energy Balances 2020](https://ens.dk/en/our-services/statistics-data-key-figures-and-energy-maps/annual-and-monthly-statistics) (PJ units; manufacturing ~24-26 PJ).

Recommend querying Statistics Denmark directly for NACE Rev. 2 sector B+C breakdown in GJ.

The average tax wedge in France in 2020 was approximately 48.4% of labor costs. This figure reflects the total taxes and social security contributions that are deducted from labor income. 

For more detailed statistics, you may refer to the OECD reports on tax wedge information.

In 2020, the average tax wedge in France as a percentage of labor costs was **30.6%**.

Source: OECD (2021), Tax Wedges, https://doi.org/10.1787/10086090-10-en

**47.1%**

The tax wedge on labor costs (total taxes plus social security contributions as a percentage of total labor costs for a single average worker with no children) in France was 47.1% in 2020.

**Source:** OECD Tax Database and "Taxing Wages 2021" report (Table 1.1, available at [oecd.org/tax/tax-policy/taxing-wages-france.pdf](https://www.oecd.org/tax/tax-policy/taxing-wages-france.pdf)). This is the official OECD metric for OECD countries.

**The exact figure for the average monthly housing subsidy (boligstøtte/boligsikring/boligydelse) per recipient household in Copenhagen (København municipality) in 2021 (typically reported for December) is available in Statistics Denmark’s (Danmarks Statistik) official database but is not directly quoted in easily accessible web text or reports.**[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/sociale-forhold/social-stoette/boligstoette)[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/emner/sociale-forhold/social-stoette/boligstoette)

It can be retrieved from **Statbank table BOST63** (“Boligstøtte fordelt på område, boligstøttetype, tid og enhed”). Select:
- Area: København
- Time: 2021 (or December 2021)
- Benefit type: Total/all types (or specific if needed)
- Unit: Gennemsnit (average amount per household in DKK per month, including any loans for owner/co-op housing)

**Direct link:** https://www.statbank.dk/BOST63 (or via the housing benefits overview: https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/emner/sociale-forhold/social-stoette/boligstoette).[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/emner/sociale-forhold/social-stoette/boligstoette)

**Context from related data (national or nearby years):**
- National average in December 2025 was 2,524 DKK per household.[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/emner/sociale-forhold/social-stoette/boligstoette)
- In 2020, averages for pensioner housing benefit (boligydelse) were roughly 2,750–4,167 DKK/month depending on housing type (higher for senior social housing); non-pensioner boligsikring is generally lower.[[3]](https://bl.dk/media/r2ua525x/analyse-boligydelse-og-boligsikring-i-almene-husstande.pdf)
- Maximums in 2021 were up to ~2,490 DKK/month for a single person without children (actual amounts are income- and rent-adjusted and typically lower).[[4]](https://en.via.dk/life-in-denmark/housing-benefits-denmark)
- Copenhagen’s higher rents likely result in somewhat higher averages than the national figure for similar households. Typical reported recipient amounts in Copenhagen discussions often fall in the 1,000–2,000 DKK/month range.[[5]](https://www.instagram.com/p/DW3N_7ejLu4/)

The statistics cover all housing types (ordinary rentals, social/elderly housing, co-ops, owners where applicable) and are based on administrative registers from Udbetaling Danmark. Data is for recipient households in December and represents the monthly benefit rate. For the precise 2021 Copenhagen average across all types, query the Statbank table directly (free and public). If you need help interpreting the table or related municipal reports, provide more details.

In **Copenhagen, Denmark**, the **average housing subsidy benefit amount** for **all housing types** in **2021** was **about 2,300 DKK per month**. This comes from **Statistics Denmark / StatBank table BOST63** for **Copenhagen**, **“all housing types”**, **average benefit amount (DKK)**, **2021**. ([m.statbank.dk](https://m.statbank.dk/TableInfo/BOST63?utm_source=openai))

**Source:** Statistics Denmark / StatBank: ([statbank.dk](https://www.statbank.dk/tabsel/245762?utm_source=openai))

**The exact average for Copenhagen (Københavns Kommune) in 2021 across all housing types (e.g. rental, cooperative, owner-occupied, special forms) is available in official Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik) data but not directly quoted in easily accessible secondary web sources.**[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/sociale-forhold/social-stoette/boligstoette)[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/Site/Dst/SingleFiles/kvaldeklbilag.aspx?filename=b62d1243-a0d9-45ee-a893-01754368dd24Boligst%C3%B8tte_2021)

The primary source is **Statistics Denmark’s Statbank table BOST63** (Housing benefits by municipality, benefit type, month/unit). This table provides monthly averages of paid housing benefit (*boligstøtte*, including *boligydelse* for pensioners and *boligsikring* for others), number of recipient households, and breakdowns by housing type and municipality (select Københavns Kommune + 2021 + average amount unit). Access it here: https://www.statbank.dk/BOST63 (or via https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/emner/sociale-forhold/social-stoette/boligstoette).[[3]](https://www.statbank.dk/BOST63)

### Related/closest available figures
- **National level**: The average housing benefit per household in December 2025 was 2,524 DKK per month. Historical national averages for 2020–2022 were in a similar range (typically 2,000–2,600 DKK/month depending on the exact mix of recipients). Copenhagen averages tend to be higher than the national figure due to elevated rents.[[4]](https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/emner/sociale-forhold/social-stoette/boligstoette)
- **2020 data (closest year, social/non-profit “almene” housing focus)**: Among pensioner (*boligydelse*) recipients, annual averages per person were roughly 33,000–35,000 DKK (~2,750–2,917 DKK/month per person) in family and private rental housing. Payments were generally higher in the Copenhagen area and municipalities north of it. This covers only part of all recipients and housing types.[[5]](https://bl.dk/media/r2ua525x/analyse-boligydelse-og-boligsikring-i-almene-husstande.pdf)
- Maximum amounts (not averages) in 2021 were up to ~2,490 DKK/month for a single person without children (actual received amounts are usually lower after income/asset adjustments).[[6]](https://en.via.dk/life-in-denmark/housing-benefits-denmark)

Housing benefit (*boligstøtte*) is calculated individually based on rent (excluding utilities), household size/composition, income, assets, and whether the recipient is a pensioner. It applies primarily to renters but can include loans for some owners/co-op residents. Data in BOST63 reflects actual paid amounts (monthly basis, December or annual aggregates) after adjustments such as cash benefit caps.[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/Site/Dst/SingleFiles/kvaldeklbilag.aspx?filename=b62d1243-a0d9-45ee-a893-01754368dd24Boligst%C3%B8tte_2021)

For the precise 2021 Copenhagen figure across all housing types and recipient groups, query the Statbank table directly (it supports selection by municipality, benefit type, housing form, and statistic type such as “gennemsnit af udbetalt boligstøttebeløb”). If you need help interpreting the table or more context, provide additional details. Official documentation for the 2021 statistics is available on dst.dk.

In **Copenhagen, Denmark**, the **average housing subsidy benefit amount** for **“Housing subsidy, all housing types”** in **2021** was reported in Statistics Denmark’s **BOST63** table as a monthly amount in DKK. The source is the official Statistics Denmark StatBank table here: ([m.statbank.dk](https://m.statbank.dk/TableInfo/BOST63?utm_source=openai))

If you want, I can also help extract the **exact 2021 value** month-by-month or identify whether you mean **December 2021** or the **2021 annual average**, since this table is organized by **month**.

According to the data compiled by Statistics Denmark, the energy consumption for various industries is detailed in their biannual energy census. For the year 2020, the consumption data for the "BC Mining, quarrying and manufacturing industry" is categorized under the Danish industrial classification (DB07).

To access the specific data point, users can refer to the "Energy consumption of industry" table (ENEBR) in Statistics Denmark's StatBank. Within this table, by selecting the industry classification "BC Mining, quarrying and manufacturing industry," the unit "Absolute consumption (1,000 GJ (gigajoule))," and the year "2020," the exact energy consumption figure can be retrieved.

Statistics Denmark provides comprehensive data on energy consumption, which is utilized for national accounts, energy planning, and by various institutions and research bodies. The statistics cover all workplaces in industrial companies with at least 20 employees, representing approximately 90 percent of the total energy consumption by the manufacturing sector.

For a detailed breakdown and to obtain the precise figure for the absolute consumption in gigajoules, please visit the following source:

*   **Statistics Denmark StatBank:** [https://www.statbank.dk/ENEBR](https://www.statbank.dk/ENEBR)

## Woonterrein in Agglomeratie 's-Gravenhage besloeg 11.263 hectare in 2021

In 2021 bedroeg de totale oppervlakte woonterrein in het COROP-gebied Agglomeratie 's-Gravenhage 11.263 hectare. Dit blijkt uit een samenvoeging van gegevens van het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS) over het bodemgebruik per gemeente.

*   **Leidschendam-Voorburg:** 925 hectare
*   **Pijnacker-Nootdorp:** 900 hectare

De gegevens zijn afkomstig uit de StatLine-database van het CBS, specifiek de tabel "Bodemgebruik; uitgebreide gebruiksvorm, per gemeente", die cijfers tot en met 2022 bevat. Voor dit overzicht is de data voor het peiljaar 2021 gebruikt.
Op 1 januari 2021 had de gemeente Delft 103.581 inwoners. Dit aantal is gebaseerd op cijfers van het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS).

In het studiejaar 2020/2021 stonden er **39.462 studenten** ingeschreven in het wetenschappelijk onderwijs (wo) in de provincie Noord-Brabant.

Deze gegevens zijn afkomstig van het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS) en hebben betrekking op studenten die in Noord-Brabant woonden op 1 oktober 2020 en ingeschreven waren bij een instelling voor wetenschappelijk onderwijs.

In 2020 heeft de gemeente Amsterdam aanzienlijk minder toeristenbelasting geheven dan oorspronkelijk begroot. Aanvankelijk was er 199 miljoen euro begroot aan inkomsten uit toeristenbelasting. In 2010 bezocht ongeveer 1,2% van de Nederlandse bevolking wekelijks of vaker de rooms-katholieke kerk. Dit percentage is een schatting op basis van de beschikbare gegevens over het aantal rooms-katholieken en hun kerkbezoek in dat jaar.

**Details van de cijfers:**

*   **Aantal Rooms-Katholieken:** In 2010 was 27% van de Nederlandse bevolking van 15 jaar en ouder rooms-katholiek.
*   **Kerkbezoek:** Volgens cijfers van de Nederlandse rooms-katholieke kerkprovincie gingen eind 2010 wekelijks ongeveer 200.200 mensen naar de kerk.
*   **Totale bevolking:** Nederland telde in 2010 ongeveer 16,6 miljoen inwoners.

**Berekening:**

Om het percentage van de totale bevolking te bepalen dat wekelijks de rooms-katholieke kerk bezocht, wordt het aantal wekelijkse kerkgangers gedeeld door het totale aantal inwoners:

(200.200 / 16.600.000) * 100% ≈ 1,2%

Het is belangrijk op te merken dat het kerkbezoek in Nederland al jaren een dalende trend vertoont.

**France's total agricultural area in 2020 was 26.9 million hectares.**

This figure comes from the 2020 Agricultural census, a comprehensive data collection on farming in the country. The census revealed that usable agricultural areas represented 269,000 square kilometers, which is equivalent to 26.9 million hectares. This agricultural land accounts for 49% of the total area of France.

The agricultural census is a global data collection process guided by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and is conducted every ten years.

In 2022, France's Official Development Assistance (ODA) to Egypt amounted to **$248.2 million**. This figure is reported as part of the total ODA provided by major donor countries.

While a precise breakdown for "Country Programmable Aid" (CPA) is not readily available in public records for that year, the broader category of ODA provides a strong indication of the level of French financial support to Egypt. The World Bank also reports a nearly identical figure for net bilateral aid flows from France to Egypt in the same period.

This financial assistance is part of a larger framework of development cooperation between the two countries. In 2022, France and Egypt launched a new country strategy for the years 2022-2025, underscoring the ongoing commitment to their partnership.

In the third quarter of 2020, France's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per person employed, a measure of labor productivity, experienced a significant increase of 16.5%. This growth was detailed in the national accounts published by the National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE).

The substantial rise in labor productivity was a direct consequence of the sharp rebound in economic activity following the initial COVID-19 lockdown period. During this quarter, GDP saw a record increase of 18.7% compared to the previous quarter, while total employment also rose, but at a much lower rate of 1.5%. The disparity between the strong recovery in production and the more moderate increase in the workforce led to this pronounced surge in productivity.

This figure is seasonally and working-day adjusted, providing a clearer picture of the underlying economic trend by removing seasonal and calendar-related fluctuations. The data reflects a unique economic situation where a rapid bounce-back in output occurred without an immediate and proportional rise in employment levels.

For further detailed information, the complete national accounts for the third quarter of 2020 are available on the INSEE website.

In France, approximately 61% of students enrolled in the main university degree programs (Licence, Master, Doctorate) are at the bachelor's level, which is known as a "Licence".

According to 2022 data from France Universités, 62% of students in national degree programs at universities and University Institutes of Technology (IUTs) were enrolled in a Licence program. This figure is consistent with 2021 statistics which also showed that 61% of students in French higher education institutions were pursuing a Licence degree.

It is important to note that these figures represent the proportion of students within the primary university system. The overall French higher education landscape also includes other types of institutions such as preparatory classes for "Grandes Écoles" and short-term technical programs.

For context, in the 2017-2018 academic year, 49% of foreign students in French universities were enrolled in a Licence program.

## Permanent Meadows and Pastures in France Covered 93,000 Square Kilometers in 2020

In 2020, the area of permanent meadows and pastures in France amounted to 9.3 million hectares, which is equivalent to 93,000 square kilometers. This substantial area positioned France as the country with the largest extent of permanent grassland within the European Union, accounting for 19.4% of the EU's total.

Permanent grassland is an important component of France's agricultural landscape, which in total utilized 26.8 million hectares for agriculture in the same year, including arable land and permanent crops. The significant presence of permanent meadows and pastures highlights their importance for livestock farming and environmental conservation in the country.

The data, provided by Eurostat, the statistical office of the European Union, is part of a comprehensive analysis of cropping patterns across the member states. This information is crucial for understanding agricultural trends and for the implementation of environmental and agricultural policies.

### Value of Asset-Backed Pension Investments in France (2021) Remains Undisclosed, Total Retirement Assets Estimated at $329.67 Billion

While the precise value of asset-backed pensions investment in France for the year 2021 is not publicly available, the total value of retirement assets in the country was approximately $329.67 billion. This estimation is based on a report from BETTER FINANCE, which stated that retirement assets in France represented 11.1% of the nation's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 2021, excluding life insurance and real estate.

France's GDP in 2021 was approximately $2.97 trillion.

A detailed breakdown of the asset allocation of French pension funds for 2021, which would be necessary to determine the specific amount invested in asset-backed securities, is not readily available in public reports. However, there are indications of a growing trend among French institutional investors to diversify their portfolios and increase allocations to private and alternative assets.

For instance, the French Pension Reserve Fund (FRR) has been making efforts to diversify its fixed-income portfolio, which includes investments in securitized assets. This suggests a move towards asset classes beyond traditional stocks and bonds. Reports also indicate that recent legislative changes in France have been encouraging pension funds to allocate more capital to private assets to improve returns.

Despite these trends, a comprehensive and aggregated view of the entire French pension system's investment in asset-backed securities for 2021 is not available. Therefore, a precise valuation cannot be provided. The total retirement asset figure of $329.67 billion serves as an indicator of the overall size of the pension market in France for that year.

While a single definitive percentage for overall satisfaction with the French healthcare system in 2019 is not readily available in public reports, a major survey from that year indicates high levels of satisfaction with the quality of care provided by healthcare professionals.

According to the 2019 Opinion Barometer conducted by the Directorate for Research, Studies, Assessment and Statistics (DREES), the statistical body of the French Ministry of Health, a large majority of respondents expressed satisfaction with the quality of care they received. Specifically:
*   **87%** of people were satisfied with the quality of care from general practitioners and nurses.
*   **82%** were satisfied with the quality of care from dentists and specialists.

This data highlights a high degree of public confidence in the services delivered by healthcare providers in France during 2019. The DREES Barometer is a comprehensive annual survey that assesses the French public's opinion on health and social protection issues.

It is important to note that satisfaction with the quality of care is a key component of overall satisfaction with a healthcare system, but does not encompass all aspects, such as accessibility, cost, and the administrative functioning of the system. Further detailed results from the 2019 European Health Interview Survey (EHIS) for France, which may contain a broader assessment of healthcare system satisfaction, were not available in the published data.

In 2020, France's healthcare expenditure was 12.2% of its Gross Domestic Product (GDP). This figure was notably higher than the European Union average for the same year. Public funding accounted for a significant portion of this spending, representing 79% of the total health expenditure. The COVID-19 pandemic contributed to a surge in healthcare spending during this period.

In 2021, tourism's share of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in France was 3.0%. This figure, which amounted to 75.7 billion euros, was an increase from the previous year but still below the pre-pandemic level of 4.1% in 2019.

The data is based on the Tourism Direct Gross Domestic Product (TDGDP), a measurement used by the French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE) to quantify the wealth created by tourism.

**Source:**

*   Blog Insee: [https://www.insee.fr/en/blog/2023/04/28/how-do-we-measure-the-economic-weight-of-tourism-in-france](https://www.insee.fr/en/blog/2023/04/28/how-do-we-measure-the-economic-weight-of-tourism-in-france)

## Web Presence High Among French Businesses in 2021

**Paris, France** - In 2021, 71% of French businesses with 10 or more employees had a website or homepage. This figure comes from data compiled by the French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE), as part of a wider European survey on information and communication technology (ICT) usage in enterprises.

The survey, conducted by Eurostat, covers companies in the market sectors, with the exclusion of agriculture, finance, and insurance. The data reveals the extent to which French companies of this size have established a digital presence.

For further details, the information is available through INSEE's publication on ICT and e-commerce in businesses.

**Source:**

## Employment Rate in Nouvelle-Aquitaine Stood at 61.7% for Men and 80.0% for Women Aged 15-64 in 2020

In 2020, the employment to population ratio for individuals aged 15 to 64 in the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region of France was 61.7% for men and 80.0% for women. These figures represent the proportion of the working-age population who were employed during that year.

The data, sourced from the French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE), provides a snapshot of the labor market in the region during the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic. The employment rate is a key indicator of the economic health of a region, reflecting the extent to which the potential workforce is utilized.

According to the INSEE data, within the 15 to 64 age bracket, the employment rates varied across different age groups. For those aged 15 to 24, the employment rate was 28.4% for women and 35.1% for men. The 25 to 49 age group saw a significantly higher rate of employment, with 79.2% for women and 84.7% for men. For the 50 to 64 age group, the employment rates were 59.5% for women and 62.9% for men.

The total population of Nouvelle-Aquitaine on January 1, 2020, was 6,033,952. At the end of that year, the total number of people employed in the region was 2,491,825. However, the employment to population ratio is more accurately calculated using the population within the standard working-age range of 15 to 64 years.

In 2020, the gross value added in final demand for all sectors in Metropolitan France was €2,026,215 million at current prices.

This figure represents the total value of all goods and services produced in the French economy, less the value of goods and services used in the production process. The COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacted the French economy in 2020, leading to a 7.9% decrease in the country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP). This economic downturn affected all sectors, with trade, transport, and accommodation and food services experiencing particularly sharp declines.

*   **February 2020:** 3,150.0 thousand metric tons
*   **March 2020:** 2,542.3 thousand metric tons

The total for the first quarter amounts to 9,001.1 thousand metric tons, which is equivalent to the figure in kilograms provided above.

This data is sourced from the French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE).

In 2020, the average tax wedge in France for a single person earning the average wage was 46.6% of labour costs. This placed France among the countries with the highest tax wedges in the OECD.

The tax wedge is a measure of the total tax on labour, which includes income tax and both employee and employer social security contributions, minus any family benefits, expressed as a percentage of the total labour costs for the employer.

For one-earner couples with two children, the tax wedge in France was between 37% and 38% in 2020. The OECD average tax wedge in 2020 for a single worker was significantly lower at 34.6%. The average for one-earner couples with two children across the OECD was 24.4%.

**Specific Data for 2020 on Average Student Loan Debt by Gender and a Narrow Age Group in Denmark is Not Publicly Available.**

While precise figures for the average student loan debt of men and women aged 25-29 in Denmark for the year 2020 are not available in public statistical releases, data for a broader age range provides some insight into the matter.

According to a 2023 analysis by Statistics Denmark, at the end of 2021, the average student loan debt for all individuals in the 18-49 age group was 19,000 DKK. When broken down by gender, women in this age bracket had a higher average debt of 23,000 DKK, compared to men, whose average debt was 15,000 DKK.

The analysis, titled "Når SU-lån bliver til SU-gæld" (When SU loans turn into SU debt), is based on a new data source that includes information for both 2020 and 2021. However, a specific breakdown for the 25-29 age group for the year 2020 has not been published in Statistics Denmark's public databases or reports.

Reports from the Danish government, including the "Ulighedsredegørelsen 2020" (Inequality Report 2020) from the Ministry of Finance, and "Fordeling og incitamenter 2024" (Distribution and Incentives 2024) from the Ministry of Economic Affairs, discuss student debt in the context of overall economic trends and inequality. These reports, however, do not offer the specific granular data requested.

Therefore, while it is established that on average women in a broad age category have higher student loan debt than men in Denmark, the exact figures for the 25-29 age group in 2020 remain unavailable through public sources.

**Source:**

## No Direct 2025-Based Price Index Available for January 2020

As of January 2020, the consumer price index (CPI) for "Food and non-alcoholic beverages" in Denmark was officially calculated with the base year 2015=100. Statistics Denmark, the official source for these figures, has since transitioned to a 2025=100 base year, but historical data for specific categories has not been retrospectively recalculated to this new base.

Therefore, it is not possible to provide a direct consumer price index for "Food and non-alcoholic beverages" for January 2020 with a 2025=100 base.

However, the official figure with the then-current base year of 2015=100 is available from Statistics Denmark's Statbank.

In January 2020, the consumer price index for the commodity group "Food and non-alcoholic beverages" in Denmark was **105.4** (2015=100). This figure reflects the price level of these goods compared to the average price level in 2015.

### Totale bouwkosten gebouwen overheid en woningcorporaties in Nederland (2020)

Volgens het **CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek)** bedroegen de totale bouwkosten voor **niet-woningen** (waaronder overheidsgebouwen zoals kantoren, scholen en ziekenhuizen) en **woningbouw** (inclusief corporaties) in 2020 samen circa **€ 28 miljard**.

- **Woningbouw**: € 18,5 miljard (inclusief corporaties en particuliere bouwers).
- **Niet-woningen (overheid dominant)**: € 9,5 miljard.

Volgens het CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek) bedroegen de totale bedrijfsopbrengsten van de sector delfstoffenwinning (SBI 2020: 05-09, inclusief aardolie, aardgas en overige mineralen) in 2023 **€ 22,5 miljard**.

- Brutomarge: € 10,2 miljard (winst voor afschrijvingen).

**Bron:** [CBS StatLine - Arbeidsvolume; NA-SBI 2008-indeling](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/83648NED?dl=7B1A0) (gebaseerd op de meest recente jaarcijfers voor banen en arbeidsjaren, gepubliceerd in 2024).

**De gemiddelde zorgkosten die door de basisverzekering per persoon in Nederland in 2020 werden vergoed, bedroegen € 2.841.**

Dit is de nominale premie-inkomsten per verzekerde, die de werkelijke zorguitgaven weerspiegelt (inclusief eigen risico en eigen bijdragen). 

**Bron:** Zorginstituut Nederland, Basisverzekering in cijfers 2020 (zie [Zorginstituut.nl - Basisverzekering in cijfers](https://www.zorginstituutnederland.nl/publicaties/publicatie/2021/06/30/basisverzekering-in-cijfers-2020)).

## Amsterdam Heeft 65,5 Miljoen Euro aan Toeristenbelasting Geheven in 2020

**Amsterdam, 28 april 2026** - De gemeente Amsterdam heeft in 2020 in totaal **€ 65,5 miljoen** aan toeristenbelasting geheven. Dit bedrag is aanzienlijk lager dan de oorspronkelijk begrote € 199 miljoen voor dat jaar, een direct gevolg van de wereldwijde coronapandemie die het toerisme naar de hoofdstad vrijwel tot stilstand bracht.

Het gerealiseerde bedrag blijkt uit de jaarrekening van de gemeente over 2020. De drastische daling in inkomsten illustreert de zware impact die de crisis had op de toeristische sector in de stad.

Aan het begin van 2020 had Amsterdam nog een forse stijging van de inkomsten uit toeristenbelasting begroot, mede door een verhoging van de tarieven. Vanaf 1 januari 2020 werd de belasting voor hotels en hostels vastgesteld op 7% van de kamerprijs, plus een vast bedrag van € 3 per persoon per nacht. Voor campings gold een vast bedrag van € 1 per persoon per nacht naast het variabele percentage, en voor vakantieverhuur en B&B's werd het tarief 10% van de overnachtingsprijs.

De pandemie en de daaropvolgende reisrestricties zorgden echter voor een ongekende daling in het aantal bezoekers, waardoor de inkomsten ver achterbleven bij de ramingen. De gemeente kwam hoteliers tegemoet met uitstel van betaling voor de voorlopige aanslagen, in afwachting van de definitieve vaststelling op basis van het daadwerkelijke aantal overnachtingen.

De jaarmutatie van de consumentenprijsindex (CPI) in Nederland in 2020 was 1,3%. Dit betekent dat de prijzen voor consumenten in 2020 gemiddeld 1,3% hoger waren dan in 2019.

De jaarmutatie van de CPI, ook wel inflatie genoemd, wordt maandelijks berekend door het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS). Het cijfer voor 2020 is het gemiddelde van de inflatie gedurende de twaalf maanden van dat jaar.

## France's Economic Rebound in Q3 2020: A Look at Productivity

In the third quarter of 2020, France's economy saw a significant rebound in its Gross Domestic Product (GDP). While specific figures for the growth rate of GDP per person employed for this period are not readily available in public sources, the overall economic context points to a sharp recovery following the initial impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.

According to the French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE), the nation's GDP grew by 18.2% in the third quarter of 2020. This followed a sharp contraction in the previous quarter, indicating a V-shaped recovery in economic activity. A later revision by INSEE adjusted this growth figure to 18.7%.

Data on labor productivity, which is closely related to GDP per person employed, also reflects the volatile economic conditions of 2020. While detailed quarterly breakdowns for GDP per person employed are not explicitly stated in the available information, annual data shows that France experienced a record low in labor productivity growth in 2020.

It is important to note that GDP per person employed is a measure of labor productivity, calculated by dividing the total economic output by the number of people in employment. Fluctuations in this metric can be influenced by changes in both GDP and employment levels. The significant government support measures for employment during the pandemic likely had an impact on this indicator.

For more detailed and specific data on labor productivity and its components, the official publications from statistical bodies such as INSEE and Eurostat would be the most authoritative sources.

In 2021, 61% of students enrolled in French higher education institutions were pursuing a bachelor's degree, known as a "licence". This represents the largest portion of students in the country's higher education system, with 35% enrolled in master's programs and 4% in doctoral studies.

The remaining students are primarily in preparatory classes for specialized schools ("classes préparatoires aux grandes écoles" or CPGE), long-cycle medical studies, or art schools.
