**Ongeveer 1,6% van de Nederlandse bevolking in 2010 was rooms-katholiek én bezocht de kerk (of een katholieke viering) één keer per week of vaker.**[[1]](https://dry.sailingissues.com/kaski-2011.pdf)

Dit cijfer komt uit tellingen van het **KASKI** (Katholiek Sociaal-Kerkelijk Instituut). In 2010 bezochten circa 266.300 mensen in het weekend een rooms-katholieke viering of dienst. Dat komt neer op ongeveer 6,4% van de geregistreerde katholieken (ruim 4 miljoen, circa 25% van de bevolking) en ongeveer **1,6% van de totale Nederlandse bevolking** (destijds circa 16,6 miljoen).[[1]](https://dry.sailingissues.com/kaski-2011.pdf)

### Belangrijke context
- Dit is een *telling* van feitelijke kerkgangers (weekendbezoek, inclusief zaterdagavond- en zondagvieringen), geen enquête onder zelfrapportage.
- CBS-enquêtes (zelfgerapporteerd kerkbezoek) laten vaak iets hogere percentages zien, maar specificeren voor exact 2010 en specifiek wekelijks rooms-katholiek bezoek geen exacte overlapcijfers. Wel was in 2010 circa 27% van de bevolking (15+) rooms-katholiek en lag het overall maandelijks kerkbezoek rond de 18%.[[2]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2025/16/daling-aandeel-mensen-dat-aangeeft-bij-religie-te-horen-stagneert)

**Bronnen** (o.a.):
- KASKI Kerncijfers Rooms-Katholieke Kerk 2011 (PDF via zoekresultaten)
- CBS StatLine / rapporten over religie en kerkbezoek (cbs.nl, o.a. “Religie in Nederland” longreads)
- Samenvattingen op pen.nl (religieuze kaart 2010-2015) en Wikipedia (Catholic Church in the Netherlands)

De secularisering zorgde daarna voor een verdere sterke daling van het katholieke kerkbezoek.

**Approximately 27 million hectares (specifically 27.4 million ha according to Eurostat, or 26.7–26.8 million ha for metropolitan France according to the national Agricultural Census).**[[1]](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Agri-environmental_indicator_-_cropping_patterns)

The most commonly cited figure for France’s **utilised agricultural area (UAA)** or *Surface Agricole Utile (SAU)* in 2020 is around **26.7–27.4 million hectares**, representing roughly half of the country’s territory. This includes arable land, permanent grassland, and permanent crops.[[2]](https://agreste.agriculture.gouv.fr/agreste-web/download/publication/publie/Pri2213-en/Primeur%202022-15_RA2020_%20Definitive-data.pdf)

- **Eurostat (EU-harmonised data)** reports **27.4 million ha** for France in 2020 (17.4% of the EU total UAA of 157.4 million ha). This breaks down roughly as 17.0 million ha arable land, 9.3 million ha permanent grassland, and 1.0 million ha permanent crops.[[1]](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Agri-environmental_indicator_-_cropping_patterns)
- **French national statistics (Agreste – 2020 Agricultural Census)** report **26.7 million ha** (26,746 thousand ha) for **metropolitan France** (a slight decline from 2010). The average farm size was 69 ha. Overseas departments add a relatively small additional area.[[2]](https://agreste.agriculture.gouv.fr/agreste-web/download/publication/publie/Pri2213-en/Primeur%202022-15_RA2020_%20Definitive-data.pdf)

Sources often round this to “approximately 28 million ha” or “about half the territory.” Slight variations come from inclusion/exclusion of overseas territories, definitions (e.g., excluding collective grazing), or rounding.[[3]](https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/cap-my-country/cap-strategic-plans/france_en)

**Primary sources:**
- Eurostat: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Agri-environmental_indicator_-_cropping_patterns
- Agreste (French Ministry of Agriculture): https://agreste.agriculture.gouv.fr/agreste-web/download/publication/publie/Pri2213-en/Primeur%202022-15_RA2020_%20Definitive-data.pdf

For the absolute latest or most specific breakdown (e.g., by region or type), consult the full Agreste census or Eurostat databases.

**Approximately $248.2 million USD in bilateral ODA (Country Programmable Aid is a core subset of this).**[[1]](https://foreignassistance.gov/cd/egypt/2022/obligations/0)

Country Programmable Aid (CPA) is the portion of Official Development Assistance (ODA) that partner countries can plan and allocate over multiple years (excluding humanitarian aid, debt relief, in-donor refugee costs, and certain other items). The most readily available figure for France–Egypt flows in 2022 is bilateral ODA of roughly **$248.2 million**, with France ranking as one of the top donors to Egypt that year (behind Japan).[[1]](https://foreignassistance.gov/cd/egypt/2022/obligations/0)

This figure comes from OECD DAC data aggregated on the U.S. Foreign Assistance dashboard (foreignassistance.gov) for Egypt in 2022. Exact CPA breakdowns by donor-recipient pair for a single year are typically found in the OECD’s CPA or Creditor Reporting System (CRS) data explorer rather than summary reports. France’s support to Egypt is channeled largely through AFD (Agence Française de Développement) via concessional loans for infrastructure, energy, water, health coverage, and private-sector projects, with cumulative commitments exceeding €4.2 billion since 2006.[[2]](https://www.afd.fr/en/countries-regions/egypt)

For the precise CPA value, consult the OECD data explorer directly (search for donor “France”, recipient “Egypt”, year 2022 under the CPA dataset): https://data-explorer.oecd.org/vis?df[ds]=dsDisseminateFinalDMZ&df[id]=DSD_CPA@DF_CRS_CPA&df[ag]=OECD.DCD.FSD&df[vs]=1.4. Individual project agreements in 2022 included tens of millions of euros in loans and grants (e.g., one deal with €52 million credit and €25.1 million grant).[[3]](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/presidential-decree-approves-deal-with-french-development-agency/)

**Main sources**: OECD DAC statistics (via foreignassistance.gov and AFD country page). Data can vary slightly between commitments vs. disbursements and current vs. constant USD.

**Approximately +16.3% quarter-on-quarter (from Q2 to Q3 2020).**[[1]](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/5392004?sommaire=5392045)[[1]](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/5392004?sommaire=5392045)

This refers to the growth rate of real apparent labour productivity (GDP/value added per person employed, or "productivité réelle apparente du travail" / "PIB par personne occupée"), seasonally adjusted. It comes from INSEE national accounts data during the COVID-19 recovery. GDP rebounded sharply (+18.7% QoQ SA in early estimates, later revised in subsequent vintages), while employment recovered more slowly, leading to strong productivity growth.[[2]](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/4984977?sommaire=4925608)

Supporting details from INSEE (index base 100 in Q1 2012 for real apparent labour productivity):
- Q2 2020: 88.3
- Q3 2020: 102.7
- Growth: (102.7 / 88.3) – 1 ≈ +16.3%.[[1]](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/5392004?sommaire=5392045)

This series aligns with quarterly national accounts (typically CVS or CVS-CJO; the exact “seasonally adjusted, not calendar adjusted” variant is a standard Eurostat/OECD adjustment option that is very close for this period). Productivity per person employed dropped sharply in Q2 2020 (due to lockdowns with job retention schemes) before rebounding strongly in Q3.[[3]](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/fichier/6010076/ndc-decembre-2021-eclairage-3.pdf)

**Main source**: INSEE (e.g., https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/5392004 and related quarterly national accounts releases such as https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/4984977). Comparable data appear in Eurostat labour productivity tables (e.g., via namq_10_lp or similar) and OECD productivity databases. Later revisions or slight differences in scope (total economy vs. non-farm market sector) or adjustment (calendar/working-day) may produce small variations, but +16.3% is the direct QoQ movement from the published indices.

**Fewer than 50% of all tertiary (higher education) students in France are enrolled in bachelor's-level programs.**[[1]](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Tertiary_education_statistics)

According to **Eurostat data for 2023**, France (along with Luxembourg, Austria, and Cyprus) is one of the few EU countries where bachelor's (or equivalent ISCED 6) students make up less than half of total tertiary enrollment. France had roughly 2.86–3 million tertiary students that year, with doctoral students comprising only 2.4% (about 69,600). Short-cycle tertiary programs (such as BTS) are relatively common.[[1]](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Tertiary_education_statistics)

In **French universities specifically** (which enroll about 54% of all higher education students, or roughly 1.6 million out of ~3 million total in 2023–24), 60% of students are in *cursus licence* (bachelor's/licence programs), 37% in master's, and 3% in doctorates. Universities represent the core of bachelor's-level university education, but the overall tertiary figure is lower due to students in short-cycle programs (e.g., BTS/STS), preparatory classes (CPGE), engineering schools, and private institutions, many of which operate at other levels.[[2]](https://publication.enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr/eesr/FR/T191/les_etudiants_en_formation_dans_l_enseignement_superieur/)

**Sources**:  
- Eurostat Tertiary Education Statistics (2023): https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Tertiary_education_statistics  
- French Ministry of Higher Education (État de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l’Innovation, 2023–24 data): https://publication.enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr/eesr/FR/T191/les_etudiants_en_formation_dans_l_enseignement_superieur/

These shares can vary slightly by year and exact definition (university-only vs. all tertiary/IS CED levels), but the pattern is consistent across recent official reports. For the most current exact breakdown, consult the latest Ministry or Eurostat data explorer.

**Approximately 93,000 km² (9.3 million hectares).**[[1]](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Agri-environmental_indicator_-_cropping_patterns)[[1]](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Agri-environmental_indicator_-_cropping_patterns)

According to Eurostat data from the 2020 Farm Structure Survey, France had 9.3 million hectares of permanent grassland (also referred to as permanent grassland and meadow for forage production, not part of regular crop rotation). This matches the FAO category of “permanent meadows and pastures,” defined as land used for five or more years for herbaceous forage crops (cultivated or wild/grazing).[[1]](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Agri-environmental_indicator_-_cropping_patterns)

Conversion: 9.3 million hectares = 93,000 km² (since 1 km² = 100 hectares). This represented about 19.4% of the EU total permanent grassland area in 2020. France’s total Utilised Agricultural Area (UAA) was around 27.4 million hectares that year.[[1]](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Agri-environmental_indicator_-_cropping_patterns)

Note that FAO/UN sources report similar but slightly varying figures (e.g., around 95,800 km² in 2021 in one UN-compiled FAO dataset), due to minor differences in definitions, survey methods, or revisions between Eurostat’s farm surveys and FAO’s land-use statistics. The 2020 Eurostat figure is the most directly applicable to the query year.[[2]](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/envstats/Questionnaires/2022/Tables/Agricultural%20Land.xlsx)

**Main source:** Eurostat Statistics Explained – Agri-environmental indicator - cropping patterns (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Agri-environmental_indicator_-_cropping_patterns). For the latest or more detailed breakdowns, check FAOSTAT Land Use domain (https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/RL).

**Approximately $307 billion USD (for the reported portion of asset-backed pension arrangements).**[[1]](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/topics/policy-sub-issues/asset-backed-pensions/PMF-2024-Preliminary-2023-Data.pdf)

According to OECD Pension Markets in Focus reports (which use the term “asset-backed pensions” for funded retirement arrangements backed by assets such as pension funds, certain insurance contracts, and schemes like FRPS and ERAFP in France), assets in these arrangements for France stood at roughly $307 billion USD at end-2021.[[2]](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/topics/policy-sub-issues/asset-backed-pensions/PMF%202025%20-%20Preliminary%202024.pdf)

This is derived from preliminary 2023 data showing $269.6 billion USD at end-2023 (8.7% of GDP, 82% system coverage), with a –12.1% change since end-2021. Reversing that change yields ~$306.7 billion for 2021. Narrower “pension fund only” figures are smaller (around 2–3% of GDP in some earlier snapshots, or ~$70–80 billion), while broader retirement savings (including more insurance products) can appear closer to 12% of GDP (~$350–390 billion range depending on the exact year and coverage).[[3]](https://www.theglobaleconomy.com/France/pension_funds_assets/)

France’s 2021 GDP was approximately $2.97 trillion USD; the pension-asset-to-GDP ratio was reported around 10–12% in nearby years (e.g. 12.18% in 2020 per World Bank data).[[4]](https://www.macrotrends.net/global-metrics/countries/fra/france/gdp-gross-domestic-product)

**Main sources:** OECD “Pension Markets in Focus” reports (e.g. preliminary 2023/2024 data PDFs available at oecd.org under asset-backed pensions) and World Bank data via theglobaleconomy.com. Exact figures can vary slightly by definition of “asset-backed” (pension funds vs. all retirement vehicles) and exchange rates. For the most current or detailed breakdown, consult the latest OECD report directly.

**47% of respondents were very or fairly satisfied with France’s healthcare system in 2019.**[[1]](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1109036/satisfaction-health-system-worldwide-by-country/?srsltid=AfmBOoo_jHOh_JTddGsf5sJxw1ZCPERuYqzBP-WT312ryUfjph50csUh)

This comes from a November–December 2019 Ipsos survey (approximately 16,000 respondents aged 16–74 across multiple countries, conducted online). The exact question was: “To what extent, if at all, are you satisfied with [COUNTRY’S] health system?” For France, the breakdown was 47% “very/fairly satisfied,” 25% “neither,” and 26% “not very/not at all satisfied” (percentages exclude “don’t know/refusal”).[[2]](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1109036/satisfaction-health-system-worldwide-by-country/)

**Source:** Statista / Ipsos survey – https://www.statista.com/statistics/1109036/satisfaction-health-system-worldwide-by-country/[[1]](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1109036/satisfaction-health-system-worldwide-by-country/?srsltid=AfmBOoo_jHOh_JTddGsf5sJxw1ZCPERuYqzBP-WT312ryUfjph50csUh)

Note that other surveys report different figures depending on the exact wording. For example, a Gallup World Poll (2016–2019) found 74% of people in France satisfied with the *availability of quality healthcare* in their local area.[[3]](https://news.gallup.com/poll/306092/satisfaction-healthcare-access-lacking-spain-italy.aspx) The Ipsos question aligns most closely with your query about satisfaction with the “healthcare system.” OECD and EU reports from the period focus more on unmet needs (which were low in France) than on overall system satisfaction.

**Approximately 12.2% of GDP.**[[1]](https://eurohealthobservatory.who.int/publications/i/france-health-system-summary-2024)[[1]](https://eurohealthobservatory.who.int/publications/i/france-health-system-summary-2024)

This figure represents France’s **current health expenditure** (including both public and private spending on healthcare goods and services) as a share of GDP in 2020. It was higher than in surrounding years (typically 11–11.5% in the late 2010s and early 2020s) largely due to elevated COVID-19-related spending.[[2]](https://www.healthsystemtracker.org/chart-collection/health-spending-u-s-compare-countries/)

The most direct source is the **European Observatory on Health Systems and Policies (WHO/Eurohealth Observatory)** report, which states: “Current health expenditure per capita in France (US$ PPP 5740) in 2020 exceeded the EU average, representing 12.2% of GDP.”[[1]](https://eurohealthobservatory.who.int/publications/i/france-health-system-summary-2024)

This aligns with data from the **WHO Global Health Expenditure Database** (the primary source for the World Bank indicator SH.XPD.CHEX.GD.ZS) and is consistent with OECD and Eurostat reporting on the 2020 pandemic spike.[[3]](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SH.XPD.CHEX.GD.ZS?locations=FR)

For the latest data or detailed breakdowns (e.g., public vs. private share), refer to:
- World Bank: https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SH.XPD.CHEX.GD.ZS?locations=FR
- OECD Health at a Glance reports
- Eurostat healthcare expenditure statistics

Note that exact figures can vary slightly by definition (e.g., current vs. total health expenditure), but 12.2% is the widely cited value for France in 2020.

**Approximately 3.0% (direct contribution).**[[1]](https://blog.insee.fr/measuring-the-economic-weight-of-tourism-in-france/)

According to INSEE (the French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies), tourism’s direct contribution to GDP—known as Tourism Direct Gross Domestic Product (TDGDP)—was **3.0% (€75.7 billion)** in 2021. This was down from 4.1% in 2019 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.[[1]](https://blog.insee.fr/measuring-the-economic-weight-of-tourism-in-france/)

This figure measures the direct value added from tourism-related activities (following UNWTO/OECD/TSA international standards) and is the official national statistic. It is lower than the broader “total contribution” (including indirect and induced effects) often reported by WTTC, which was around 6–7% (€158–162 billion) in 2021.[[2]](https://wttc.org/news/frances-travel-and-tourism-could-surpass-pre-pandemic-levels-in-2023)

**Primary source:** INSEE – “Measuring the economic weight of tourism in France” (Insee Focus no. 297, April 2023): https://blog.insee.fr/measuring-the-economic-weight-of-tourism-in-france/ (or full note at https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/7455206).

**71%.**[[1]](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/6667021?sommaire=6667157)

According to Insee (using Eurostat data from the 2021 ICT survey in enterprises), 71% of French companies with 10 or more employees in the mainly market sectors (excluding agriculture, finance, and insurance) had a website or homepage in 2021. This places France in the lower third of EU countries (EU average: 78%). For very large enterprises, the figure was 94% in both France and the EU.[[1]](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/6667021?sommaire=6667157)

**Source:** Insee — “TIC dans les entreprises en Europe” (based on Eurostat): https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/6667021?sommaire=6667157.[[1]](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/6667021?sommaire=6667157)

The scope matches the query exactly (enterprises with 10+ employees). Data for this indicator are typically collected via harmonised EU enterprise ICT surveys.

**Approximately €45,130 (average annual wages in current euros).**[[1]](https://www.statista.com/statistics/416204/average-annual-wages-france-y-on-y-in-euros/?srsltid=AfmBOoq7PlYLngV7dy7JMKaAkIzs8bo30IemvcQUVSEStoT_K-7XvcLJ)

This figure comes from Statista’s time series on average annual wages in France (1990–2024, in current prices), which reports 45.13 thousand euros for 2021. It reflects gross wages per full-time equivalent employee in the total economy and follows an uneven upward trend (from ~€33,650 in 1990 to €44,910 in 2024).[[2]](https://www.statista.com/statistics/416204/average-annual-wages-france-y-on-y-in-euros/)

For context from official French sources:
- INSEE reports a mean annual “revenu salarial” (net of social contributions) of €22,420 across all employees in 2021, or €30,290 in full-time equivalent (EQTP) terms. This covers private and public sectors (excluding certain groups like apprentices).[[3]](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/8242353?sommaire=8242421)

The higher ~€45k figure aligns with OECD-style average annual wage indicators used for international comparisons. Figures can vary by exact definition (gross vs. net, private sector only, inclusion of bonuses, or FTE adjustment). For the most current or detailed breakdowns, check INSEE or OECD directly.[[4]](https://www.oecd.org/en/data/indicators/average-annual-wages.html)

**Key sources**:  
- Statista: https://www.statista.com/statistics/416204/average-annual-wages-france-y-on-y-in-euros/  
- INSEE (Portrait social): https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/8242353

**Approximately 3.71 million (precisely 3,713,426 as of 1 January 2020).**[[1]](https://www.insee.fr/en/statistiques/2382597?sommaire=2382613)

This figure covers **France including Mayotte** (total population ≈ 67.06 million) and comes from INSEE’s official “Population by sex and age on 1st January 2020” table. It is obtained by summing the single-year-of-age data for ages 25 through 29 (birth cohorts 1994 to 1990).[[1]](https://www.insee.fr/en/statistiques/2382597?sommaire=2382613)

### Breakdown (approximate, from the same source):
- Males: ≈ 1.835 million
- Females: ≈ 1.879 million
- Total: 3,713,426

**Source**: INSEE (French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies) — detailed table available at: https://www.insee.fr/en/statistiques/2382597 (or the French version). Minor discrepancies of a few dozen people between male + female and published totals are typical in such rounded official statistics.[[1]](https://www.insee.fr/en/statistiques/2382597?sommaire=2382613)

For the most up-to-date or metropolitan-France-only figures, check the latest INSEE demographic balance sheet.

**In the context of economic statistics, "value added in final demand" most commonly refers to indicators from the OECD's Trade in Value Added (TiVA) database.** These break down how much domestic and foreign value added (from different countries and industries) is embodied in a country's final demand (household/government consumption, investment/GFCF, etc.). Key related metrics include:[[1]](https://www.oecd.org/en/topics/sub-issues/trade-in-value-added.html)[[2]](https://stats.oecd.org/wbos/fileview2.aspx?IDFile=afa5c684-c31d-49dd-87db-6fd674f29a43)

- **Domestic value added embodied in foreign final demand** (exports of VA).
- **Foreign value added embodied in domestic final demand** (imported VA content of French final demand).
- **Origin of value added in final demand** (FDVA_BSCI), which shows the full breakdown by source country/industry for final demand in France.

These data are available in the OECD TiVA database (2025 edition or earlier releases covering up to 2020). Specific absolute values (in USD millions) or shares for France in 2020 require querying the interactive OECD data explorer or downloading the datasets, as they are not summarized in static public highlights. Figures and percentages by industry/partner for 2020 appear in OECD country notes (e.g., foreign VA content of exports or domestic VA in foreign final demand as % of total VA), but exact aggregates vary by indicator.[[3]](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/topics/policy-sub-issues/trade-in-value-added/tiva-2023-FRA.pdf)

**A closely related aggregate is France's total Gross Domestic Product (GDP), which equals total gross value added generated in the economy to satisfy final demand (adjusted for trade).** France's GDP in 2020 was approximately **$2.648 trillion USD** (a decline from 2019 due to the COVID-19 pandemic).[[4]](https://www.macrotrends.net/global-metrics/countries/fra/france/gdp-gross-domestic-product)

For precise TiVA numbers (e.g., foreign VA share in French final demand or bilateral breakdowns), consult the primary source:  
- OECD TiVA page and data explorer: https://www.oecd.org/en/topics/sub-issues/trade-in-value-added.html (or https://data-explorer.oecd.org/ with the TiVA dataset).[[1]](https://www.oecd.org/en/topics/sub-issues/trade-in-value-added.html)

French national accounts from INSEE provide complementary GVA data by industry (in euros), but they do not use the exact "in final demand" global supply-chain decomposition.

**9,057,000,000 kg (or 9.057 billion kg / 9,057 thousand tonnes).**[[1]](https://www.statistiques.developpement-durable.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/2020-05/datalab_essentiel_213_conjoncture_energetique_2020_t1_mai2020.pdf)

This is the total for **carburants routiers** (supercarburants/gasoline + road gazole/diesel deliveries to the road sector/transports routiers) in France for Q1 2020 (January–March). It represents about 49.8% of total petroleum product consumption that quarter and was down 7.1% vs. Q1 2019 (or ~8.3% on a corrected basis), with a sharp contraction in March due to early COVID-19 lockdowns (gazole/diesel –25.3%, supercarburants –21.4% in March alone vs. March 2019). Breakdown (in thousand tonnes): supercarburants ≈ 1,845 kt (–0.4%); road gazole ≈ 7,212 kt (–8.7%, ~79.6% of road fuels).[[1]](https://www.statistiques.developpement-durable.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/2020-05/datalab_essentiel_213_conjoncture_energetique_2020_t1_mai2020.pdf)

**Source**: SDES (Service des Données et Études Statistiques, now under the French Ministry of Ecological Transition), *Conjoncture énergétique – Premier trimestre 2020* (May 2020 data release). Direct PDF: https://www.statistiques.developpement-durable.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/2020-05/datalab_essentiel_213_conjoncture_energetique_2020_t1_mai2020.pdf.[[1]](https://www.statistiques.developpement-durable.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/2020-05/datalab_essentiel_213_conjoncture_energetique_2020_t1_mai2020.pdf)

These are official “livraisons” (deliveries to the domestic market), reported in mass. CPDP (now under UFIP Énergies et Mobilités) publishes complementary monthly bulletins on carburants routiers, often in volume (m³), which align with these figures. Density-based conversion from volume would be needed for exact kg if starting from m³ data, but the SDES report already provides mass. For the most precise or updated revisions, check the latest SDES/CPDP archives.

**46.6% of labour costs (for a single worker earning the average wage, with no children).**[[1]](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2021/04/taxing-wages-2021_a735042c/83a87978-en.pdf)

This is the standard OECD measure of the “average tax wedge,” which includes income tax, employee and employer social security contributions, minus any cash benefits, expressed as a percentage of total labour costs to the employer.[[2]](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/2021/04/taxing-wages-2021_a735042c.html)

According to the OECD’s *Taxing Wages 2021* report (which presents 2020 data), France’s tax wedge for this category was 46.6% in 2020. This placed it among the highest in the OECD, behind Belgium (51.5%), Germany (49.0%), and Austria (47.3%). The OECD average in 2020 was 34.6%.[[1]](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2021/04/taxing-wages-2021_a735042c/83a87978-en.pdf)

**Source**: OECD *Taxing Wages 2021* (available at: https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/2021/04/taxing-wages-2021_a735042c.html or the full PDF report). Data for later years (e.g., ~46.9–47.2% in 2023–2025) shows it remained relatively stable at a high level.

**Approximately 2,719,968 dwellings with registered population (also called occupied or beboede boliger) as of 1 January 2020.**[[1]](https://www.danskindustri.dk/om-di/kontakt-os/presse/arkiv/pressemeddelelser/2021/4/singler-star-for-nasten-hele-vaksten-i-boligmassen/)[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/borgere/boligforhold/boligbestanden)

This figure comes from Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik) data via their housing stock statistics (table BOL101 and related releases). “Dwellings with registered population” refers to units in the Building and Dwelling Register (BBR) that have at least one person registered at the address in the Central Population Register (CPR) on the reference date (typically 1 January). It excludes vacant dwellings, holiday homes/cottages without registered residents, and other unoccupied units.[[3]](https://www.dst.dk/Site/Dst/SingleFiles/kvaldeklbilag.aspx?filename=ad6d7ed6-437e-40d2-ba0f-5ed63be95b58Census_of_Housing_2020)

A contemporary report citing official DST figures states there were 2,748,568 such dwellings on 1 January 2021, reflecting an increase of 28,600 from 1 January 2020—yielding the 2,719,968 figure.[[1]](https://www.danskindustri.dk/om-di/kontakt-os/presse/arkiv/pressemeddelelser/2021/4/singler-star-for-nasten-hele-vaksten-i-boligmassen/) The DST housing stock page confirms this category and provides interactive charts and StatBank access (e.g., BOL101) showing the trend across years including 2020.[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/borgere/boligforhold/boligbestanden)[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/borgere/boligforhold/boligbestanden)

For the most up-to-date or detailed breakdowns (by region, dwelling type, tenure, etc.), consult the official StatBank table directly: https://www.statbank.dk/BOL101 or the housing stock overview at https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/borgere/boligforhold/boligbestanden. Numbers increase gradually each year (reaching ~2.87 million by 2026 in later data).

**There is no publicly available exact figure for the average outstanding study loans (SU-gæld) specifically for men and women aged 25-29 in Denmark in 2020.** The closest official data comes from Danmarks Statistik (Statistics Denmark) in their August 2023 analysis “Når SU-lån bliver til SU-gæld,” which uses register data as of 31 December 2021 (including many 2020 graduates).[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/analysepdf/51788)

### Key findings from the report (18–49 age group, which includes 25–29):
- **Average SU debt per person** (including people with zero debt):  
  - Women: **23,000 DKK**  
  - Men: **15,000 DKK**  
  - Overall: **19,000 DKK** (18% of this age group had any SU debt).[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/analyser/51788-naar-su-laan-bliver-til-su-gaeld)

- **Average among those who actually had SU debt**:  
  - Women: **119,000 DKK**  
  - Men: **95,000 DKK**.[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/analysepdf/51788)

The average debt peaks around age 30 (roughly 30,000 DKK per person including zeros), as many people in the late 20s/early 30s have recently completed their studies and have had limited time to repay. Debt is therefore likely similar for the 25–29 group — probably in the **20,000–28,000 DKK** range on average (including zeros), though exact single-year or 25–29-specific gender splits are not published in the report.[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/analysepdf/51788)

### For recent graduates (those finishing a qualifying education in 2020 or 2021):
These individuals (many aged around 25–29) had the following average remaining SU debt at the end of 2021 (little repayment had occurred yet):
- Medium-length higher education (mellemlang videregående uddannelse): **≈68,000–69,000 DKK** overall (women ≈72,000 DKK, men ≈63,000 DKK).
- Long higher education (lang videregående uddannelse): **≈57,000 DKK**.[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/analysepdf/51788)

**Source**: Danmarks Statistik analysis (2023, data for 2021): https://www.dst.dk/analyser/51788-naar-su-laan-bliver-til-su-gaeld (PDF: https://www.dst.dk/analysepdf/51788).[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/analyser/51788-naar-su-laan-bliver-til-su-gaeld)

More granular tables may exist in Statistikbanken.dk under “Formue og gæld” (wealth and debt statistics) with SU-lån breakdowns by age and gender, but they were not directly accessible in the searched summaries. Danish SU loans are generally modest compared to many other countries because the system combines grants with limited loans. For the most up-to-date or custom figures, check directly with Statistics Denmark or their database.

**Approximately 2,207 DKK per household per month nationally in 2021 (specific Copenhagen figure not directly available in secondary sources).**[[1]](https://politiken.dk/danmark/forbrug/boligoghaven/art8842755/Titusinder-lejere-har-allerede-justeret-deres-husleje-for-at-f%C3%A5-boligst%C3%B8tte)

In 2021, roughly 600,000 Danish households received housing benefit (*boligstøtte*, which includes *boligydelse* for pensioners and *boligsikring* for others). The national average payout was about 2,207 DKK per household per month.[[1]](https://politiken.dk/danmark/forbrug/boligoghaven/art8842755/Titusinder-lejere-har-allerede-justeret-deres-husleje-for-at-f%C3%A5-boligst%C3%B8tte)[[2]](https://www.altinget.dk/by/ministersvar/72048)

This figure covers all recipient types and housing (primarily rentals, including social/almene, private, youth housing, etc.). Totals paid out were around 15–16 billion DKK for the year.[[3]](https://www.atp.dk/dokument/udbetaling-danmark-aarsrapport-2021)

### Copenhagen-specific data
No easily accessible published report gives the exact average monthly amount for Copenhagen municipality (Københavns Kommune) in 2021. Rents are significantly higher in Copenhagen than the national average, and housing benefits are partly tied to actual rent levels (up to certain caps, adjusted for household size and income). Therefore, the average benefit in Copenhagen was **likely higher** than the national 2,207 DKK/month.[[4]](https://bl.dk/media/r2ua525x/analyse-boligydelse-og-boligsikring-i-almene-husstande.pdf)

**Primary source for the exact Copenhagen 2021 figure (all housing/benefit types):** Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik) table **BOST63** (Housing benefits by geographical region/municipality, benefit type, time, and unit — includes averages, medians, and number of recipients). You can query it interactively here: https://www.statbank.dk/BOST63 (select municipality “København”, year 2021, appropriate benefit types and “average payment” unit).[[5]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/sociale-forhold/social-stoette/boligstoette)

Documentation: https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/sociale-forhold/social-stoette/boligstoette

Related analyses (e.g., for social housing in 2020) show annual per-person averages of roughly 33,000–50,000 DKK depending on housing type (≈ 2,750–4,167 DKK/month), with higher payouts in the Greater Copenhagen area, but these are not the overall household average for all types in 2021.[[4]](https://bl.dk/media/r2ua525x/analyse-boligydelse-og-boligsikring-i-almene-husstande.pdf)

For the most accurate/current calculation for a specific household, use the official calculator on borger.dk. Data for later years (e.g. 2023 national average around 2,300–2,500 DKK/month) shows similar patterns.

**16,335,000 litres (or 16,335 thousand litres) of pure alcohol.**[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/51342)[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/51342)

This figure represents recorded sales of beer subject to excise duties in Denmark in 2020, converted to pure alcohol volume. It comes from official tax-based statistics (table ALKO6 or equivalent in Statbank Denmark).[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/erhvervsliv/handel/salg-af-alkohol-og-tobak)

For context, total pure alcohol sales (all beverages) that year were approximately 44–46 million litres. The primary source is Statistics Denmark:  
- Main page: https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/erhvervsliv/handel/salg-af-alkohol-og-tobak (links to Statbank tables like ALKO6/ALKO4).[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/erhvervsliv/handel/salg-af-alkohol-og-tobak)  
- 2024 news release with historical table (including 2020): https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/51342.[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/51342)

Data are available back to the 1920s in their Statbank. Note that these figures cover recorded sales and may not include all unrecorded consumption or border trade. Per-capita totals (e.g., ~7.6 litres in 2019) are also published but differ slightly by age group (15+ or 18+).

**Around 17,300 new passenger cars (personbiler) were registered in Denmark in January 2020 (seasonally adjusted figure from Danmarks Statistik).**[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/29923)

The actual split was 9,437 to households and 7,844 to businesses (summing to 17,281). This comes from the official “Nyregistrerede motorkøretøjer januar 2020” report.[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/29923)

“Motor vehicles” (motorkøretøjer) technically includes passenger cars, vans (varebiler), trucks (lastbiler), and buses, but the main publicized monthly figure and headline statistic focuses on passenger cars. Exact totals for vans/trucks/buses in January 2020 were not highlighted in the primary sources. For comparison, February 2020 saw 15,005 new passenger cars.[[2]](https://via.ritzau.dk/pressemeddelelse/13589189/nyregistrerede-personbiler-i-februar-2020?publisherId=13559753)

**Main sources:**
- Danmarks Statistik (DST) report: https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/29923 (or the statistics page https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/transport/transportmidler/nyregistrerede-og-brugte-biler)
- Mobility Denmark monthly releases (e.g., February 2020 summary referencing January trends): https://mobility.dk/nyregistreringer/

For the most precise or up-to-date breakdowns (including by fuel type or vehicle category), check the interactive Statbank at https://www.statistikbanken.dk/bil5 or Mobility Denmark’s archive. Note that 2020 overall was affected by the early COVID-19 pandemic and changing registration taxes.

**In 2020, there were 2,536,619 unique persons who were members of sports organizations/associations (foreningsidræt) in Denmark.**[[1]](https://www.dif.dk/media/1dtjxahu/dif_idraetten_i_tal_2020.pdf)

This is the official deduplicated figure (each person counted only once, even if they belonged to clubs under multiple organizations). It comes from the Central Foreningsregister and is reported in the official DIF publication *Idrætten i tal 2020*.[[1]](https://www.dif.dk/media/1dtjxahu/dif_idraetten_i_tal_2020.pdf)

### Key details:
- **Gross figures** (with overlaps): DIF had 1,918,811 members, DGI had 1,634,180, and Dansk Firmaidræt had 343,479.[[1]](https://www.dif.dk/media/1dtjxahu/dif_idraetten_i_tal_2020.pdf)
- The unique total dropped by 128,288 members from 2019 (2,664,907), largely due to COVID-19 lockdowns.[[1]](https://www.dif.dk/media/1dtjxahu/dif_idraetten_i_tal_2020.pdf)

**Source**: Official report “Idrætten i tal 2020” by Danmarks Idrætsforbund (DIF): https://www.dif.dk/media/1dtjxahu/dif_idraetten_i_tal_2020.pdf

Statistics Denmark (DST) publishes similar unique membership statistics via their sports club register, which align with these figures.

**Approximately 89,499,000 GJ (or 89,499 TJ).**[[1]](https://ens.dk/sites/ens.dk/files/Statistik/energy_statistics_2020.pdf)[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/miljoe-og-energi/energiforbrug-og-energipriser/energiforbrug)

This figure refers to the energy consumption of Denmark’s manufacturing industry (NACE/DB07 sections C, branches 10–33) including parts of mining and quarrying/raw material extraction (branches 08–09, corresponding to NACE section B). This matches the “BC Mining, quarrying and manufacturing industry” description. The data comes from Statistics Denmark’s bi-annual survey (primarily enterprises with >20 employees) and is published in the Danish Energy Agency’s *Energy Statistics 2020* report.[[3]](https://ens.dk/sites/ens.dk/files/Statistik/energistatistik2019_dk-webtilg.pdf)

In the report, manufacturing consumption rose 1.2% in 2020 versus 2019 (consistent with COVID-19 impacts on industry overall), reaching 89,499 TJ in the relevant table column (units are TJ; 1 TJ = 1,000 GJ). This aligns with the series shown on the Statistics Denmark energy consumption page (e.g., 92,083 TJ reported for 2024 with a –5% change from two years prior).[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/miljoe-og-energi/energiforbrug-og-energipriser/energiforbrug)

Note that this is generally **final/direct energy consumption** from the manufacturing survey. The related Statistics Denmark energy accounts table (ENE3H) reports *gross* energy consumption in GJ by industry (including B Mining and quarrying with subcategories like extraction of oil/gas, gravel/stone, and C Manufacturing); it attributes conversion/transmission losses to end-users and may yield a somewhat different total.[[4]](https://m.statbank.dk/TableInfo/ENE3H)[[5]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/miljoe-og-energi/groent-nationalregnskab/energi-og-emissionsregnskaber)

For the precise 2020 value from ENE3H or the full survey breakdown by energy type, consult the interactive Statbank tables directly (e.g., ENE3H for gross consumption by industry/energy type/time, or tables linked from dst.dk such as 20519/ENEBR/ENETYPE). Data for 2020 reflects observed values; climate-adjusted figures may differ slightly. Total Danish gross energy consumption was on the order of ~650–700 PJ around that time, with industry (including BC) forming a significant but declining share.[[6]](https://ens.dk/sites/ens.dk/files/Statistik/energy_statistics_2021.pdf)

Sources: Danish Energy Agency (*Energy Statistics 2020* PDF and later editions), Statistics Denmark (energy consumption pages and Statbank ENE3H/related tables).

**Het exacte aantal is te vinden in de officiële CBS-tabel.**[[1]](https://opendata.cbs.nl/#/CBS/nl/dataset/84826NED/table?searchKeywords=communicatie)

De beste bron is de **CBS StatLine-tabel 84826NED**: “Ontslagen werknemers door faillissement; geslacht, leeftijd, bedrijfstak”. Hierin kun je precies selecteren op:

- Jaar: 2019
- Leeftijd: 15 tot 75 jaar
- Geslacht: Totaal mannen en vrouwen

**Directe link**: [https://opendata.cbs.nl/#/CBS/nl/dataset/84826NED/table](https://opendata.cbs.nl/#/CBS/nl/dataset/84826NED/table) (of via opendata.cbs.nl zoeken op “84826NED”).[[2]](https://opendata.cbs.nl/#/CBS/nl/dataset/84826NED/table?searchKeywords=energie)

Uit openbare CBS-cijfers weten we dat in het **tweede kwartaal van 2019 alleen al circa 5.700 werknemers** hun baan verloren door faillissement van hun werkgever. Het jaartotaal voor 2019 ligt hoger (naar verwachting rond de 20.000–25.000, afhankelijk van de overige kwartalen), maar het precieze cijfer voor de volledige periode en de gevraagde leeftijdsgroep staat in bovenstaande tabel.[[3]](https://www.fiscount.nl/publicaties/arbeid-en-recht/cbs-cijfers-tweede-kwartaal-2019-5700-mensen-op-straat-na-faillissement/)

**Bronnen**:
- CBS StatLine (tabel 84826NED)
- CBS-bericht over Q2 2019 (via o.a. Fiscount en Risk & Business)

Als je hulp wilt bij het uitlezen van de tabel of een specifiekere uitsplitsing (bijv. per bedrijfstak of geslacht), laat het weten.

**90,0% (jaargemiddelde voor 2020).**[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2025/12/arbeidsparticipatie-25-tot-45-jarigen-stagneert)

Volgens CBS-gegevens was de **netto arbeidsparticipatie** (aandeel van de bevolking met betaald werk) van mannen van 25 tot 45 jaar in 2020 **90,0%**. Dit is het jaargemiddelde. Voor het specifieke 1e kwartaal van 2020 (voor de volle impact van de coronacrisis) is geen apart kwartaalcijfer direct gevonden in openbare overzichten, maar het lag rond dit niveau (in 2019 was het jaargemiddelde 90,5%).[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2025/12/arbeidsparticipatie-25-tot-45-jarigen-stagneert)

### Belangrijke bronnen
- CBS-artikel “Arbeidsparticipatie 25- tot 45-jarigen stagneert” (met tabel jaarcijfers 2003–2024): https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2025/12/arbeidsparticipatie-25-tot-45-jarigen-stagneert
- StatLine-tabel “Arbeidsdeelname; kerncijfers” (85264NED) voor gedetailleerde kwartaal- en jaargegevens naar geslacht en leeftijd: https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/85264NED of https://opendata.cbs.nl/#/CBS/nl/dataset/85264NED/table

Je kunt in StatLine zelf de filters instellen op “Mannen”, “25 tot 45 jaar” en “2020 1e kwartaal” voor het meest precieze cijfer.

**Het gemiddelde ziekteverzuimpercentage in Nederland in 2020 was 4,75%.**[[1]](https://www.hr-kiosk.nl/hoofdstuk/arbeidsinactiviteit/cijfers-landelijk-en-bedrijven)

Dit cijfer komt van het CBS en is hoger dan in de jaren ervoor, vooral door de coronapandemie (met name in het eerste en vierde kwartaal).

### Per kwartaal (CBS):
- 1e kwartaal 2020: **5,2%**
- 2e kwartaal 2020: **4,5%**
- 3e kwartaal 2020: **4,4%**
- 4e kwartaal 2020: **4,9%**[[2]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/visualisaties/dashboard-arbeidsmarkt/werkenden/ziekteverzuim)

**Bron:** Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS) – dashboard ziekteverzuim en gerelateerde StatLine-tabellen (dataset 80072NED).  
Je vindt de meest actuele versie hier: [https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/visualisaties/dashboard-arbeidsmarkt/werkenden/ziekteverzuim](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/visualisaties/dashboard-arbeidsmarkt/werkenden/ziekteverzuim).

**Ongeveer 1,5 miljoen (exacte cijfer voor Q1 2021 is te vinden in de CBS-tabel; in Q2 2021 waren het er 1.538.595).**[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/visualisaties/dashboard-economie/bedrijven)

Volgens gegevens van het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS) bestaat het overgrote deel van de Nederlandse bedrijven uit eenmanszaken (bedrijven met precies 1 werkzaam persoon, inclusief de eigenaar). De beschikbare tabel op het CBS-dashboard begint met het tweede kwartaal van 2021 op 1.538.595 bedrijven in deze categorie. Het aantal groeide in de loop van 2021 verder (naar circa 1,58 miljoen in Q3 en 1,62 miljoen in Q4).[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/visualisaties/dashboard-economie/bedrijven)

De precieze waarde voor het **1e kwartaal van 2021** (peildatum begin van het kwartaal) staat in de officiële StatLine-tabel “Bedrijven; bedrijfstak” (tabel 81589NED of 81588NED). Hierin kun je filteren op “A-U Alle economische activiteiten” en de periode “2021 1e kwartaal” bij de kolom “Bedrijfsgrootte 1 werkzaam persoon (aantal)”.[[2]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/81588NED)

**Bronnen en links (direct te raadplegen):**  
- CBS Dashboard Bedrijven: https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/visualisaties/dashboard-economie/bedrijven  
- StatLine-tabel (interactief, downloadbaar als CSV): https://opendata.cbs.nl/#/CBS/nl/dataset/81589NED/table of https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/81589NED  

“Werkzame personen” omvat zowel eigenaren als eventuele medewerkers. De cijfers betreffen een momentopname aan het begin van het kwartaal en zijn gebaseerd op administratieve bronnen van de KvK en Belastingdienst. Voor de meest actuele of gedetailleerde (per sector) data kun je de tabel zelf filteren.

**Het exacte percentage is niet direct in één nieuwsbericht te vinden, maar wel in de officiële CBS-statistiek.**[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/82190ned)

De juiste bron is de CBS StatLine-tabel **82190NED**: “Bedrijfsgegevens; omzetontwikkeling (stijgers-dalers), SBI 2008”. Hierin staat per kwartaal en bedrijfstak (inclusief ‘J Informatie en communicatie’) het percentage bedrijven dat aangeeft hogere omzet te hebben gerealiseerd ten opzichte van hetzelfde kwartaal een jaar eerder (de “stijgers”), plus het percentage met lagere omzet (“dalers”) en het saldo.[[2]](https://opendata.cbs.nl/statline/#/CBS/nl/dataset/82190NED/table?dl=4EF04)

**Link naar de tabel (selecteer periode 2020 3e kwartaal en sector J):**  
https://opendata.cbs.nl/statline/#/CBS/nl/dataset/82190NED/table

In dezelfde conjunctuurdata (tabel 84142NED) stond voor Q3 2020 een omzetindex van 107,7 (2015=100) en een negatief saldo van -5,0 voor de omzetverwachting in de sector Informatie & Communicatie.[[3]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/84142NED)

**Bronnen**  
- CBS StatLine 82190NED (stijgers/dalers per branche en kwartaal)  
- CBS Conjunctuurbeeld per bedrijfstak (84142NED)  

Je kunt de tabel filteren op de gewenste periode en branche voor het precieze percentage bedrijven met omzetstijging.

**Volgens het CBS zijn er in de periode 2021-2023 ongeveer 17.000 banen verloren gegaan door verplaatsing van bedrijfsactiviteiten naar het buitenland.**[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/86229NED)

Dit betreft “banen verloren”: banen die zijn geschrapt of omgezet naar andere taken in Nederland als gevolg van verplaatsing. Tegelijkertijd ontstonden er circa 3.000 banen door deze verplaatsingen (netto verlies dus rond de 14.000 banen).[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/86229NED)

### Specificaties
- **Hooggeschoold**: 6.000 banen verloren
- **Niet-hooggeschoold**: 10.000 banen verloren

**Belangrijke context**:
- Het gaat om marktgerichte actieve bedrijven met gemiddeld **minstens 50 werkzame personen** in de sectoren nijverheid/energie en commerciële dienstverlening.
- Volledig vertrokken bedrijven en slapende eenheden zijn niet meegenomen.
- Banen worden hier gedefinieerd als een verzameling taken en verantwoordelijkheden (niet als individuele personen).
- De cijfers zijn voorlopig (*).

Bron: CBS-tabel “Banen; verplaatsing buitenland, verloren en ontstaan” (bijgewerkt 27 januari 2026): https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/86229NED.[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/86229NED)

Dit is de meest recente en officiële statistiek over dit onderwerp. Oudere cijfers (bijv. uit 2018) liggen in dezelfde orde van grootte, maar hebben een andere periode en scope.

**Ruim 37.000 buitenlandse multinationals (bedrijven met uiteindelijke zeggenschap in het buitenland) waren in 2020 actief in Nederland.**[[1]](https://www.taxlive.nl/nl/documenten/nieuws/meer-buitenlandse-multinationals-vestigen-zich-in-nederland/)

Dit cijfer komt uit CBS-onderzoek naar multinationals: bedrijven waar de *uiteindelijke zeggenschap* (Ultimate Controlling Institutional unit, UCI) buiten Nederland ligt en die vestigingen hebben in meerdere landen (inclusief Nederland). Het aantal is tussen 2015 en 2020 met ongeveer 15% gestegen.[[1]](https://www.taxlive.nl/nl/documenten/nieuws/meer-buitenlandse-multinationals-vestigen-zich-in-nederland/)

De vraag gaat specifiek over **vestigingen** (lokale bedrijfseenheden, niet alleen de juridische entiteiten/bedrijven). Hiervoor is de exacte tabel de CBS StatLine-publicatie:

- **Vestigingen van bedrijven; zeggenschap, bedrijfstak, regio** (tabel 81996NED).  
  Link: [https://opendata.cbs.nl/statline/#/CBS/nl/dataset/81996NED/table](https://opendata.cbs.nl/statline/#/CBS/nl/dataset/81996NED/table)[[2]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/81996NED)

In deze tabel kun je voor 2020 het totaal aantal vestigingen selecteren waarbij de uiteindelijke zeggenschap in het buitenland ligt (naar SBI-bedrijfstak en regio). Gegevens zijn beschikbaar vanaf 2010. Ter vergelijking: in 2024* lag dit aantal rond de 39.750 (op een totaal van circa 2,5 miljoen vestigingen).[[2]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/81996NED)

**Gerelateerde tabel (voor bedrijven, niet vestigingen):**  
“Buitenlandse zeggenschap bedrijven in Nederland; 2008-2020” (81358NED) → [https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/81358ned](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/81358ned).[[3]](https://opendata.cbs.nl/statline/#/CBS/nl/dataset/81358ned/table?ts=1728982257796)

**Bronnen**  
- CBS StatLine (tabellen 81996NED en 81358NED).  
- CBS-publicaties en nieuws over buitenlandse multinationals (o.a. 2022-berichten over de 37.000-cijfers).  

Je kunt de tabellen zelf filteren op jaar 2020, “Buitenland” / “Uiteindelijke zeggenschap buitenland” en “Totaal Nederland” voor het precieze getal.

**In 2020 immigreerden ongeveer 109.000 personen met een EU/EFTA-nationaliteit (andere Europese nationaliteit, exclusief Nederlanders) naar Nederland.** Dit was een daling van 15.000 ten opzichte van 2019.[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2021/29/vooral-minder-immigranten-van-buiten-de-eu-in-2020)

Ter vergelijking: 
- Totaal immigreerden er circa 221.000 personen (inclusief terugkerende Nederlanders, ruim 50.000).
- Van de niet-Nederlandse immigranten (171.000) kwamen er 61.700 uit landen buiten de EU/EFTA.[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2021/29/vooral-minder-immigranten-van-buiten-de-eu-in-2020)

Deze cijfers komen uit de officiële migratiestatistiek van het **Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS)**. EU/EFTA omvat de EU-landen plus Noorwegen, IJsland, Liechtenstein en Zwitserland. Het CBS maakt onderscheid tussen Nederlandse nationaliteit, EU/EFTA en niet-EU/EFTA.[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2021/29/vooral-minder-immigranten-van-buiten-de-eu-in-2020)

**Bron:**  
https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2021/29/vooral-minder-immigranten-van-buiten-de-eu-in-2020

Meer gedetailleerde tabellen vind je in CBS StatLine (tabel 84808NED voor EU/EFTA-immigranten). De coronamaatregelen in 2020 speelden een rol bij de daling.

**In 2020 waren er 50.233 huwelijkssluitingen in Nederland.**[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/visualisaties/dashboard-bevolking/levensloop/trouwen)

Dit cijfer komt rechtstreeks van het **Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS)**. Het is een duidelijke daling ten opzichte van voorgaande jaren, vooral door de coronamaatregelen waardoor veel bruiloften werden uitgesteld of afgeblazen. Ter vergelijking: in 2022 waren het er weer 70.608.[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/visualisaties/dashboard-bevolking/levensloop/trouwen)

**Let op:** Dit betreft alleen huwelijkssluitingen (huwelijken). Daarnaast werden er in 2020 nog 24.136 geregistreerde partnerschappen gesloten.

**Bron:**  
CBS Dashboard “Trouwen”: https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/visualisaties/dashboard-bevolking/levensloop/trouwen

Je kunt de meest gedetailleerde en actuele tabellen vinden via StatLine op de website van het CBS.

**In 2020 werden in Nederland 168.681 levendgeboren kinderen geregistreerd.**[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/85722NED)[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/85722NED)

Dit cijfer komt uit de officiële kerncijfers over geboorte van het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS). Het betreft alle levendgeborenen onder de Nederlandse bevolking (ongeacht zwangerschapsduur). 

**Bron:** [CBS – Geboorte; kerncijfers](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/85722NED)

**Eind 2020 waren er 78.911 statushouders (erkende vluchtelingen) in Nederland.**[[1]](https://www.indexmundi.com/facts/netherlands/indicator/SM.POP.REFG)

Dit cijfer komt uit de statistieken van de UNHCR (United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees). Het betreft de geregistreerde refugee population onder UNHCR-mandaat aan het einde van het jaar (december 2020), naast circa 11.892 asielzoekers die nog wachtten op een beslissing.[[2]](https://www.amnesty.nl/wat-we-doen/themas/vluchtelingen-en-asielzoekers/vluchtelingen-en-asielzoekers-in-nederland)

### Belangrijke context
- CBS-rapporten richten zich vooral op *nieuwe* verblijfsvergunningen asiel (in 2020 ongeveer 18.000 verleend) en cohorten vanaf 2014, niet op het totale bestand (stock) op een specifiek moment.[[3]](https://longreads.cbs.nl/asielenintegratie-2024/statushouders-huisvesting-en-integratie/)
- Het UNHCR-cijfer is de meest direct beschikbare en breed geciteerde bron voor het totale aantal erkende vluchtelingen/statushouders in Nederland op dat moment.
- Let op: “statushouders” wordt in beleidscontext soms smaller gebruikt (bijv. alleen recent gehuisveste personen via taakstellingen van gemeenten). Het UNHCR-getal betreft de bredere groep met vluchtelingenstatus.

**Bronnen** (o.a.):
- UNHCR Global Trends / IndexMundi: https://www.indexmundi.com/facts/netherlands/indicator/SM.POP.REFG
- Amnesty International Nederland: https://www.amnesty.nl/wat-we-doen/themas/vluchtelingen-en-asielzoekers/vluchtelingen-en-asielzoekers-in-nederland
- CBS Longreads over asiel en integratie (voor context over instroom): https://longreads.cbs.nl/asielenintegratie-2024/statushouders-huisvesting-en-integratie/

Voor de meest actuele of gedetailleerde cohortcijfers kun je het beste rechtstreeks op CBS StatLine of de jaarlijkse “Asiel en integratie”-publicaties kijken.

**19,2 maanden (voor nieuwbouweengezinswoningen).**[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/86260NED)

Dit is de gemiddelde doorlooptijd van de eerste bouwvergunning tot de oplevering (voltooiing) van nieuwbouwwoningen. Voor eengezinswoningen in Nederland in 2020 rapporteert het CBS een gemiddelde van 19,2 maanden (mediaan 17,1 maanden).[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/86260NED)

**Bron:** CBS-tabel “Doorlooptijden nieuwbouw woningen en niet-woningen” (https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/86260NED).[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/86260NED)

### Let op
Dit betreft **nieuwbouw**. De verkooptijd (tijd te koop) van *bestaande* eengezinswoningen lag in 2020 volgens de NVM veel lager, rond de 30–50 dagen (ruim een maand) afhankelijk van het type (vrijstaande woningen duurden langer).[[2]](https://www.nvm.nl/media/sdikprzh/bijlage-i-analyse-woningmarkt-2020-4.pdf)

Als je de verkooptijd van bestaande woningen bedoelt in plaats van de bouwtijd van nieuwbouw, laat het me weten voor een preciezere specificatie per woningtype.

**Volgens CBS StatLine (tabel 83706NED: Bouw; bouwkosten nieuwbouw naar bestemming, bouwfase, opdrachtgever) lagen de geschatte totale bouwkosten voor gebouwen (nieuwbouw) van de Overheid of Woningcorporaties in 2020 rond de 220.070–263.520 (x 1.000 euro, dus circa €220–264 miljoen), afhankelijk van de bouwfase (bijv. ontvangen orders, aanvang of gereed).**[[1]](https://opendata.cbs.nl/#/CBS/nl/dataset/83706NED/table?searchKeywords='wijk%2002%20werkhoven')

De exacte cijfers variëren per fase (ontvangen orders, bouw begonnen, oplevering) en bestemming (woningen vs. utiliteitsgebouwen). Voor de volledige jaarcijfers en breakdowns kun je de interactieve tabel raadplegen en filteren op “Totale bouwkosten gebouwen” + “Overheid of Woningcorporaties” + jaar 2020.[[1]](https://opendata.cbs.nl/#/CBS/nl/dataset/83706NED/table?searchKeywords='wijk%2002%20werkhoven')

**Bron:** CBS StatLine – https://opendata.cbs.nl/#/CBS/nl/dataset/83706NED/table (of via https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/83706NED).[[2]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/statline/recente-cijfers)

Deze tabel geeft de geschatte bouwkosten op basis van bouwvergunningen en orders (excl. BTW). Voor bredere investeringscijfers (nationale rekeningen) kun je eventueel tabel 84091NED raadplegen, maar die is minder specifiek voor “bouwkosten gebouwen”.

**Volgens officiële CBS-cijfers (tabel 83673NED) liggen de gemiddelde bouwkosten voor nieuwbouwwoningen (op basis van de bouwsom uit bouwvergunningen, exclusief BTW) rond de €1.150–€1.200 per m² in recente jaren.** Voor precies 2021 is de gedetailleerde split voor koopwoningen in de huidige online tabel niet meer direct zichtbaar (de tabel toont nu vooral data vanaf 2023 met €1.157 per m² voor koopwoningen in Nederland over rolling 12-maandsperioden). Wel melden CBS-publicaties dat de bouwkosten in 2021 ongeveer 15% hoger lagen dan in 2020.[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/83673NED)

**Bron:** CBS StatLine – Kerncijfers nieuwbouwwoningen; bouwkosten, inhoud, regio: https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/83673NED (en bijbehorende publicaties Bouwen en Wonen). De bouwkosten per m² zijn berekend als totale bouwsom (excl. BTW) gedeeld door het totale aantal m² van zuivere woningbouwprojecten.

**Let op:** Dit CBS-cijfer betreft de gerapporteerde bouwsom uit vergunningen en ligt vaak lager dan de werkelijke/realiseerde bouwkosten (inclusief bijkomende kosten, winstmarge, installaties en BTW). Praktijkrichtprijzen van aannemers en architecten voor nieuwbouw koopwoningen lagen in die periode vaak hoger:

- Standaard rijtjeswoning: circa €1.800–€2.400 per m² (incl. BTW, afhankelijk van specificaties).
- Vrijstaande of luxere woningen: €2.200–€4.000+ per m².

Deze schattingen komen uit bouwkostenadviseurs en architectenbureaus en zijn sterk afhankelijk van type woning, duurzaamheidseisen (BENG/gasloos), regio en afwerkingsniveau. Tussen 2018 en 2021 stegen de bouwkosten significant (rond de 30% volgens onderzoek van Bouwend Nederland), vooral door energienormen en materiaalkosten.[[2]](https://www.bouwendnederland.nl/nieuws/algemeen/hoge-huizenprijzen-door-regelgeving-en-winsten-grondeigenaren)

Voor de meest actuele of specifieke cijfers (bijv. per regio of woningtype) raadpleeg ik de CBS StatLine-tabel direct of een bouwkostenadviseur. Wil je data voor een ander jaar, type woning of inclusief/exclusief BTW? Laat het weten.

**De winning van aardgas (productie) in Nederland in 2020 bedroeg circa 800-900 PJ (schatting op basis van trend).**[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2020/20/minder-steenkool-en-meer-aardgas-verbruikt-in-2019)[[2]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/83140NED)

Volgens CBS-cijfers daalde de winning in 2019 al naar 1.010 PJ (een daling van ruim 150 PJ ten opzichte van 2018). In 2020 zette deze daling door door het beleid om de winning uit het Groningenveld sterk af te bouwen (i.v.m. aardbevingen). In 2021 lag de winning rond de 840 PJ (volgens EBN-gegevens: circa 649 PJ land + 192 PJ zee).[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2020/20/minder-steenkool-en-meer-aardgas-verbruikt-in-2019)[[3]](https://www.ebn.nl/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/EBN-Infographic-2023-energie-in-cijfers-A4.pdf)

Exacte jaarcijfers staan in de CBS-tabel **Energiebalans; aanbod, omzetting en verbruik** (StatLine, tabel 83140NED). Daar kun je de kolom “Winning” voor “Aardgas” in PJ opzoeken voor 2020. Link: [https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/83140NED](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/83140NED).[[2]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/cijfers/detail/83140NED)

Ter vergelijking: het **verbruik** van aardgas lag in 2020 rond de 1.317 PJ. Nederland werd in die periode al steeds meer afhankelijk van import.[[4]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/visualisaties/tijdlijn-historische-energie/1959-aardgas)

Bronnen: CBS (nieuwsbericht 2020 over 2019 en StatLine Energiebalans), EBN-infographics (gebaseerd op CBS-data). De winning is sindsdien sterk verder gedaald (rond de 300 PJ in 2024).

**De netto productie van elektriciteit uit kernenergie in Nederland in 2020 bedroeg 3.865 GWh, oftewel 3.865.000.000 kWh (3,865 miljard kWh).**[[1]](https://www.epz.nl/app/uploads/2023/10/EPZ-jaarverslag-2020.pdf)

Specifieke kernenergiecijfers liggen rond de 3,9 TWh (zoals in 2019), wat goed matcht met dit EPZ-rapport en tabellen van andere bronnen zoals Wikipedia (die op officiële data gebaseerd lijken).[[2]](https://www.cbs.nl/en-gb/news/2026/11/production-and-export-of-electricity-at-record-levels)

**Bron:** EPZ Jaarverslag 2020 (https://www.epz.nl/app/uploads/2023/10/EPZ-jaarverslag-2020.pdf). Het gaat hier om de gerapporteerde productie (meestal netto of net-to-grid in dit soort verslagen).

### Belangrijke context
- Het CBS hanteert de periode 0–22/23 jaar.
- Vanaf 2021 is er een trendbreuk door een sterk uitgebreide populatie van jeugdhulpaanbieders die gegevens aanleverden. Daardoor zijn de cijfers vanaf 2021 hoger dan in voorgaande jaren en niet 1-op-1 vergelijkbaar.
- In latere CBS-tijdreeksen (2024–2026) komt het definitieve cijfer voor 2021 soms naar voren als circa 469.700–470.000 na revisies.[[3]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2026/18/minder-jongeren-met-jeugdzorg-in-2025)

**Bron:** Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS) – rapport *Jeugdhulp 2021* (29 april 2022): [https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/longread/rapportages/2022/jeugdhulp-2021](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/longread/rapportages/2022/jeugdhulp-2021). Zie ook de kerncijfers op StatLine (dataset 85099NED).

**In 2020 waren er in Nederland in totaal 122.050 gestarte adviezen bij Veilig Thuis.**[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2022/17/meer-adviezen-maar-minder-meldingen-kindermishandeling-en-huiselijk-geweld)

Dit betreft de som van de twee halfjaren: 58.575 in de eerste helft en 63.475 in de tweede helft van 2020.[[2]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/longread/rapportages/2024/impactmonitor-aanpak-huiselijk-geweld-en-kindermishandeling-2024/4-vergroting-bereik-veilig-thuis)

### Wat zijn “gestarte adviezen”?
Dit zijn adviestrajecten die Veilig Thuis start nadat iemand (slachtoffer, omstander of professional) contact opneemt met zorgen over (vermoedens van) huiselijk geweld of kindermishandeling. Veilig Thuis geeft dan op maat gemaakte adviezen, tips en eventuele doorverwijzingen. Het verschilt van formele “meldingen”.

Deze landelijke cijfers komen uit de halfjaarlijkse CBS-rapportage *Beleidsinformatie Veilig Thuis*. Het aantal adviezen lag in 2020 rond de 122 duizend en is daarna verder gestegen (bijv. circa 134.000 in 2021).[[1]](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2022/17/meer-adviezen-maar-minder-meldingen-kindermishandeling-en-huiselijk-geweld)

**Bronnen** (CBS en NJI):  
- https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2022/17/meer-adviezen-maar-minder-meldingen-kindermishandeling-en-huiselijk-geweld  
- https://www.nji.nl/databanken/cijfers/cijfers-over-veilig-thuis  

Voor de meest actuele of gedetailleerde tabellen kun je het beste rechtstreeks op CBS StatLine of de NJI-databank kijken.

**Approximately 1.9 million DKK for ages near retirement (peaking at 1.9 million DKK median for 65-69 year olds in 2020).**[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/udgivelser/NytHtml?cid=35154)

According to Statistics Denmark’s “Formue og gæld 2020” release (published December 2021, covering end-of-2020 data under the 2020 definition of net wealth, which includes unquoted shares and certain public debt), the median net wealth rises strongly with age, peaks at **1.9 million DKK for the 65-69 age group**, and then declines after 70-74 as people draw down savings in retirement. Average (mean) wealth peaked at 2.8 million DKK per person in the same 65-69 group.[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/udgivelser/NytHtml?cid=35154)

The release does not explicitly quote the median for the exact 60-64 bracket (unlike releases for 2019 data, which gave 1.7 million DKK for 60-64, or 2021 data, which gave 2.013 million DKK for 60-64). Given the age pattern and wealth growth in 2020 (driven by financial markets and deposits), the 60-64 median was slightly below the 65-69 peak but in a similar range.[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/nyt/32217)

For the precise 60-64 figure, see the detailed tables in Statistikbanken (e.g., via formue1, FORMUE11, or age-grouped median tables such as LABY12). These allow custom extractions by age, year, and definition (2014 vs. 2020). Main source: https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/udgivelser/NytHtml?cid=35154 (and the associated Statbank links on the page).[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/udgivelser/NytHtml?cid=35154)

Note that median figures are generally more representative of a “typical” person than averages, as a small number of very high-wealth individuals pull the mean higher. Figures are in nominal DKK at the end of the year.

**5,822,763 (on 1 January 2020).**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_Denmark)

This is the official figure for the population of Denmark on the first day of 2020 Q1 (January 1), as published by Statistics Denmark. It is the standard reference date used for annual “Population 1. January” and “Population at the first day of the quarter” (table FOLK1A / BEFOLK2) statistics.[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/borgere/befolkning/befolkningstal)

For comparison, the figure for 1 January 2019 was 5,806,081. You can view the full time series directly in Statistics Denmark’s Statbank (search for FOLK1A or BEFOLK2).[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/borgere/befolkning/befolkningstal)

**Main source:** Statistics Denmark – https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/borgere/befolkning/befolkningstal (and the linked Statbank tables).

**1,515 (virtually all from non-Western countries).**[[1]](https://ecre.org/denmark-parliament-votes-blind-on-externalising-asylum-procedures-and-protection-obligations/)

In 2020, Denmark recorded 1,515 new asylum applications (the gross figure, described as the lowest ever registered, heavily impacted by COVID-19 border closures). This matches official government statistics cited by sources such as the Danish Refugee Council’s Refugees Welcome site and reports referencing the Ministry of Immigration and Integration (UIM).[[2]](https://refugeeswelcome.dk/en/information/facts/numbers-statistics/how-many-are-coming-and-from-where/)

"Non-Western" in Danish statistics generally refers to countries outside the EU/EEA, UK, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Switzerland, and a few others. Virtually all asylum applicants that year came from countries such as Syria, Afghanistan, Eritrea, Iran, Iraq, and similar origins, which fall squarely into the non-Western category. Applications from Western countries are negligible or zero in these statistics.[[3]](https://researchbriefings.files.parliament.uk/documents/CBP-10391/CBP-10391.pdf)

Slight variations appear in some reports (e.g., ~1,547), likely due to differences in counting methods (first applications vs. all, or net vs. gross), but 1,515 is the consistently cited official total for new applications in 2020.[[4]](https://www.chathamhouse.org/2021/06/denmarks-immigrants-forced-out-government-policies)

**Main sources**: Official figures from the Danish Ministry of Immigration and Integration (UIM), as referenced in reports from refugeeswelcome.dk and ECRE (European Council on Refugees and Exiles). For detailed tables by nationality, see annual "International Migration – Denmark" reports from the Ministry or Statistics Denmark (dst.dk) asylum statistics.

**83.4 years (for the 2020/2021 period).**[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nyt/38326)

According to official statistics from Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik), the period life expectancy at birth for newborn girls (0-year-old females) in the 2020/2021 period was 83.4 years. This represents a small decline of 0.2 years compared to the prior period (before the full COVID-19 impact), while male life expectancy was 79.6 years. Denmark publishes these figures as two-year averages (e.g., 2020/2021 or 2024–2025, when it reached 83.9 years for girls).[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/emner/borgere/befolkning/middellevetid)

These values come from Denmark’s Civil Registration System and health registers. International sources like WHO or the World Bank often report similar or slightly different modeled estimates for single calendar years, but Statistics Denmark’s data is the primary official source for the country.[[3]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/borgere/befolkning/middellevetid)

For the latest or more detailed breakdowns (including by region), see the Statistics Denmark page: https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/borgere/befolkning/middellevetid or their news release at https://www.dst.dk/nyt/38326.

**Approximately 2.8 million (with a seasonally adjusted employment rate of 73.8% for ages 15-64).**[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/31839)

This figure comes from Statistics Denmark’s Labour Force Survey (Arbejdskraftundersøgelsen, AKU/LFS), which classifies people as “employed” according to ILO standards (the “labour force with employment status employed”). The survey covers ages 15–89 (with the main rate reported for 15–64). Absolute levels are available in their interactive Statbank (e.g., table AKU101K or related tables at https://www.statbank.dk/20318), while press releases often highlight the rate and changes.[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/arbejde-og-indkomst/befolkningens-arbejdsmarkedsstatus/arbejdskraftundersoegelsen-aku)

Note that there was a methodological break in the EU LFS series in 2021, so comparisons with later quarters should be made cautiously. For the exact quarterly series (seasonally adjusted or not, by age group or industry), consult the Statbank directly or Moody’s Analytics summaries (sourced from Statistics Denmark).[[3]](https://www.economy.com/denmark/labor-force)

**Primary source:** Statistics Denmark LFS page and Q1 2021 release – https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/arbejde-og-indkomst/befolkningens-arbejdsmarkedsstatus/arbejdskraftundersoegelsen-aku (and the specific news release PDF for Q1 2021).

**The overall median disposable income (ækvivaleret disponibel indkomst) in Denmark in 2020 was 267,900 DKK.**[[1]](https://www.ae.dk/tema/2022-06-de-laveste-indkomster-halter-fortsat-efter-resten)[[1]](https://www.ae.dk/tema/2022-06-de-laveste-indkomster-halter-fortsat-efter-resten)

Specific median income figures for the 25-29 age group are not directly quoted in easily accessible news reports or summaries for 2020. However, Danmarks Statistik (Statistics Denmark) publishes detailed breakdowns—including medians for personal income, disposable income, wages, and other types—by age group (including 25-29 years) in their interactive Statistikbanken database.[[2]](https://nst.statistikbank.dk/statbank5a/SelectVarVal/Define.asp?MainTable=INDKP201&PLanguage=0&PXSId=0&wsid=cftree)

**Key tables to check:**
- **INDKP201** (Hovedtabel personindkomster): Covers median values (Median (kr.)) by income type (e.g., disposable income), sex, age (including 25-29 år), and year. Select 2020 and the desired income type. Link: https://www.statbank.dk/INDKP201
- Wage/earnings table **LONS50**: Includes median hourly earnings (median fortjeneste) for 25-29 year olds by sector, sex, etc. Link: https://m.statbank.dk/TableInfo/LONS50
- Income distribution overview (with links to age-specific poverty tables that reference the median): https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/emner/arbejde-og-indkomst/indkomst-og-loen/indkomstfordeling

Younger age groups (like 25-29) typically have lower medians than the population average due to students, early-career workers, and entry-level positions. For the exact 2020 median in DKK for this group, query the tables above directly (free and public). Data comes from register-based statistics (e.g., income registers).[[3]](https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/emner/arbejde-og-indkomst/indkomst-og-loen/indkomstfordeling)

If you need averages instead of medians, or data for a different income definition (gross personal income vs. disposable), let me know for further refinement.

**144,589 students (general upper secondary / gymnasiale uddannelser).**[[1]](https://www.statista.com/statistics/576918/number-of-students-in-upper-secondary-education-in-denmark/?srsltid=AfmBOorbRSR3nJf-emAOlkzuoCoTaG4P3mRiqr06wUd4U--AEvZ972zo)

This figure is the official count as of 1 October 2020 from Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik), which reports enrollment in general upper secondary programmes (such as STX, HF, HTX, and HHX) on that exact date each year. It aligns with the “pr. 1. oktober” methodology used in their statistics (e.g., table UDDAKT30 / Statistikbanken) and is consistent with later figures (e.g., ~143,000 in 2025).[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/uddannelse-og-forskning/fuldtidsuddannelser/ungdomsuddannelser)

Note that this refers specifically to general upper secondary education (university-preparatory programmes). Vocational upper secondary/VET programmes are tracked separately (typically ~100,000–110,000 students) and are not included in this total.[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/uddannelse-og-forskning/fuldtidsuddannelser/ungdomsuddannelser)

**Primary source:** Statistics Denmark (via Statista summary): https://www.statista.com/statistics/576918/number-of-students-in-upper-secondary-education-in-denmark/ and https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/emner/uddannelse-og-forskning/fuldtidsuddannelser/ungdomsuddannelser. For raw data, see Statistikbanken table UDDAKT30.

**The specific figures for innovation expenditures on the acquisition of machinery, equipment, software, and buildings (or closely related categories such as “Køb af maskinel, udstyr og software til innovation”) by information and communication companies (NACE section J / “Informations- og kommunikationsvirksomheder”) in Denmark in 2020 (or the 2018–2020 reference period) are not published in aggregated news releases or PDFs.**[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nyt/32244)[[2]](https://www.dst.dk/nytpdf/32244)

These detailed breakdowns are available in **Statistics Denmark’s (Danmarks Statistik) interactive statistical database** under table **INN21**: “Erhvervslivets innovationsudgifter efter branche og udgiftstype” (Business innovation expenditures by industry and type of expenditure). The unit is 1,000 DKK.[[3]](https://www.statistikbanken.dk/statbank5a/SelectVarVal/Define.asp?MainTable=INN21&PLanguage=%200&PXSId=0&wsid=cftree)[[3]](https://www.statistikbanken.dk/statbank5a/SelectVarVal/Define.asp?MainTable=INN21&PLanguage=%200&PXSId=0&wsid=cftree)

**Direct link to the table:** https://www.statistikbanken.dk/INN21 (or https://www.statistikbanken.dk/tabsel/252299).[[4]](https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/udgivelser/NytHtml?cid=38274)

### How to retrieve the data
- Select year/reference period around **2020** (the innovation survey covering 2018–2020 was released in 2021).[[1]](https://www.dst.dk/nyt/32244)
- Select industry: **Informations- og kommunikation**.
- Select expenditure type: Look for “Køb af maskinel, udstyr og software til innovation” (purchase of machinery, equipment and software for innovation). Buildings are often included in tangible-asset categories or listed separately in the breakdown.[[5]](https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/emner/uddannelse-og-forskning/forskning-udvikling-og-innovation/innovation)
- Other related tables include INN22 (innovative enterprises by industry).

The main innovation statistics page is: https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/emner/uddannelse-og-forskning/forskning-udvikling-og-innovation/innovation.[[5]](https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/emner/uddannelse-og-forskning/forskning-udvikling-og-innovation/innovation)

**Note:** These figures come from the Community Innovation Survey (CIS)-style survey following Oslo Manual guidelines and are based on a sample, so they carry some uncertainty. Total innovation expenditure (all types) for Danish businesses is published in news releases, but the exact asset-acquisition breakdown for the ICT sector requires the statbank query.[[6]](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/cache/metadata/en/inn_cis12_esms.htm)

For the precise number in DKK, query the table directly at the link above. If you need help interpreting the output or data for another year/breakdown, provide more details.
